policy.purpose: Phase-3 owner ADRs freeze the public contract of each capability before any implementation or dependency exit may start. An ADR is a decision record, not an implementation licence.
policy.no_loss_rule: No ADR may authorize removal or narrowing of an accepted public API, generic extension point, Cargo feature, binary, accepted format, wire protocol, platform cell, diagnostic, third-party integration, or documented user journey. Additive redesign is permitted; erasure is not.
policy.keep_default: When a complete owned replacement is disproportionate or its parity is unproven, the required terminal decision is KEEP_UNTIL_PARITY with cutover_state KEEP_INCUMBENT.
policy.no_compatibility_shims: Asupersync is pre-1.0 with no external users to protect. Preserved surfaces stay because the capability is real, not because a deprecated alias is kept alive. ADRs may not introduce compatibility shims or wrapper facades for deprecated APIs.
policy.authority_rule: An ADR carries decision authority only for the capability IDs mapped to its bead by bead_mapping_rules in the capability registry. Cross-cutting capability mentions are compatibility obligations, never primary evidence ownership.
policy.evidence_rule: Every ADR names the exact unit-test owner, no-mock E2E owner, and stable scenario IDs that must be green before its capability may cut over. Naming planned evidence is not the same as having run it.
policy.truthful_baseline_rule: An ADR must record the capability as it actually is at claim time, including gaps, quarantined surfaces, and dead code paths. Freezing an aspirational surface is a defect; known gaps are recorded so they cannot silently widen.
policy.aggregate_rule: asupersync-dep-p3-api-adrs-h3jspm.13 may not close while any roster row is PENDING or any resolved row carries an UNKNOWN capability, format, feature, platform, interoperability, or user-journey field.

surface_state_meanings.SHIPPED_OWNED: Implemented in asupersync's own code and reachable in a production build.
surface_state_meanings.SHIPPED_VIA_DEPENDENCY: Reachable in production, but the working path runs through the third-party dependency under review. Removing that dependency removes the capability.
surface_state_meanings.SHIPPED_OWNED_INPROCESS: Owned code exists and is reachable, but it stops at the process boundary; there is no production path to the external consumer.

surface_state_meanings.NOT_SHIPPED: Does not exist today. Recorded so an ADR cannot silently imply that it does.

adrs.title: Preserve generic SerdeCodec JSON + MessagePack + Bincode while versioning owned artifacts
adrs.decision_summary: All four SerializationFormat discriminants stay, SerdeCodec stays generic over arbitrary Serialize and DeserializeOwned types, and the custom-codec injection points stay. Owned artifact schemas are versioned additively on top of the encoders already in use. The claim-time source read shows the Rev-3 proposal to drop the public Bincode and MessagePack variants is not an API-narrowing question at all: MessagePack is the on-disk encoding of every trace file and replay trace, and Bincode encodes distributed-snapshot vector clocks under a pinned legacy config. Removing either makes existing persisted artifacts unreadable. The versioning the bead asks for partly exists already and is preserved rather than invented: trace files carry an eleven-byte magic plus a u16 container version with a forward-rejecting check, replay carries an exact-match schema version, crash packs carry both a current version and a minimum supported floor, and TypeRegistry records a name, version and schema hash per type.

alternatives_considered.option: Replace the public Bincode and MessagePack variants with JSON plus purpose-built codecs, per the Rev-3 plan.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Presented as an API narrowing, it is really a persisted-format break. rmp-serde writes trace metadata and every trace event; bincode with the legacy config writes distributed-snapshot vector clocks. Dropping the variants strands the existing corpus. It also deletes a genuine downstream extension capability, which the no-loss gate forbids independently.

alternatives_considered.option: Keep the encoders internally but remove the variants from the public SerializationFormat enum.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: SerializationFormat is public, re-exported at asupersync::types, and is a parameter of the public Serializer and Deserializer traits and of the TypedEncoder and TypedDecoder constructors. The discriminants are also frozen on the wire as bytes 1, 2, 3 and 255 in the typed-symbol header, so removing a variant breaks both compilation and stored bytes.

alternatives_considered.option: Drop SerializationFormat::Custom, since SerdeCodec itself rejects it.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Custom is not dead. Byte 255 round-trips through the header parser, and the discriminant is what a downstream Serializer or Deserializer implementation claims when injected through with_serializer or with_deserializer. SerdeCodec declining it is the intended division of labour, and the downstream consumer fixture already asserts that rejection as contract.

alternatives_considered.option: Migrate persisted traces and snapshots to one owned canonical format and retire the incumbent readers.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Permitted only as an additive format with a reader for the existing corpus. The persisted capability is PRESERVE_AND_REPLACE_IF_PARITY and BLOCKED_PENDING_EVIDENCE, and its no-claim boundary states that canonicalizing future artifacts does not authorize dropping any accepted historical artifact without migration and rollback proof.

alternatives_considered.option: Write an owned serializer and deserializer covering the full Serde data model, then drop rmp-serde and bincode.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Not rejected in principle, but the bar is the complete Serde data model, the accepted byte formats, matching error and resource semantics, and comparable usability, validated against synthesized arbitrary-type consumers, the persisted corpus, a malformed corpus and migration readers. KEEP is explicitly correct if the marginal benefit does not justify reimplementing a complete serializer and deserializer.

preserved_public_symbols.note: The exact re-export set. None reach the crate root, so both asupersync::types:: and asupersync::types::typed_symbol:: are stable paths and both are frozen.

SerdeCodec is a unit struct with zero inherent methods; all behavior comes from two blanket impls bounded only by T: Serialize and T: DeserializeOwned. with_serializer and with_deserializer are the concrete custom-codec injection points. register and schema_hash are the per-type versioning machinery.

The persisted trace container: an eleven-byte magic, a u16 container version, a compression flag, and explicit bounds on metadata, event, chunk and preallocation sizes. Payloads inside are MessagePack. Several of these, including HEADER_SIZE, FLAG_COMPRESSED and the MAX_ bounds, are reachable only by the long path and are public API regardless.

ReplayTrace::to_bytes returns Result<Vec<u8>, rmp_serde::encode::Error>, so a format crate appears directly in a public return type, and ReplayTraceError holds a #[from] rmp_serde::decode::Error variant.

Pretty JSON with deterministic version-stamped filenames and atomic temp-plus-rename writes. This is the only artifact in the crate with an explicit backward-compatibility floor as well as a current version, and it is the model the other artifacts should generalize. The entire writer surface is reachable only by the long path.
There is no disk format here. serde_json appears in exactly one place, feeding an FNV content hash, so the JSON encoder is a hash-determinism dependency rather than a storage dependency.

The only production bincode user outside typed_symbol.rs. Vector clocks encode under bincode::config::legacy() for a deterministic binary representation; decode failure maps to an explicit invalid-vector-clock error.

preserved_feature_flags.name: default
preserved_feature_flags.effect: None of serde, serde_json, rmp-serde or bincode is optional, so all three real format paths are available even to a consumer building with default-features = false. This row pins that: feature-gating any format would be capability narrowing.
preserved_feature_flags.no_tokio_guarantee: None of the four serialization crates introduces a tokio edge.

preserved_feature_flags.name: trace-compression
preserved_feature_flags.effect: Enables LZ4 block framing for trace chunks, signalled by FLAG_COMPRESSED in the container header. Uncompressed trace files must remain readable whether or not this is enabled.

preserved_feature_flags.name: serialization-golden-harnesses
preserved_feature_flags.effect: Gates the golden-artifact and protocol-serialization harnesses. Recorded because the capability registry names it, and because SER-GAP-04 shows those harnesses do not currently cover the codec.

preserved_feature_flags.name: cli
preserved_feature_flags.effect: Provides the trace-inspection CLI, the operator-facing consumer of the persisted trace format, and transitively enables trace-compression so any CLI build reads and writes LZ4 trace files.

preserved_surfaces.wire_encoder: serde_json, rmp-serde, and bincode (package bincode-next) behind one dispatch
preserved_surfaces.note: Unlike the protobuf codec, this error surface is already owned: every failure is stringified into SerializationError or DeserializationError, and the format crates appear only as closure parameter annotations. SerdeCodec could swap backends with no public API change, which is exactly why the capability is about the accepted BYTES and the data model rather than about types.
Owned code with no dependency on any format crate. Byte 255 round-trips through the header parser so a downstream codec can own the Custom discriminant.
The container and its versioning are already owned; only the payload encoders are third-party. Format discriminants are frozen as header bytes and an unknown byte is rejected explicitly.

preserved_surfaces.wire_encoder: MessagePack via rmp-serde, optionally LZ4-framed chunks
preserved_surfaces.note: This is why the format variants are not merely an enum. Two independent version checks apply: the container version is forward-rejecting and backward-accepting, while the embedded replay schema version is exact-equality and therefore strictly stricter.

preserved_surfaces.transport: atomic temp-plus-rename file writes through an explicit writer capability
preserved_surfaces.note: The only versioned artifact with a backward-compatibility floor, validated as a closed range. There are no ambient filesystem writes; persistence requires the writer capability.

preserved_surfaces.wire_encoder: bincode legacy config for vector clocks, inside an owned framed layout
preserved_surfaces.note: The legacy config is a deliberate wire-compatibility pin, not an incidental default. Changing it silently changes the bytes and breaks interchange.

preserved_surfaces.wire_encoder: serde_json, used only as input to an FNV content hash
preserved_surfaces.note: There is no lab snapshot disk format. The subtle hazard is that the integrity hash is computed over serde_json output, so changing the JSON encoder silently changes every content hash and invalidates verify_integrity for any previously stored hash.
No owned serializer or deserializer covering the Serde data model exists. Recorded so this ADR cannot be read as implying a partial replacement is available.
Version checks reject incompatible artifacts but nothing converts an older artifact into a newer or canonical form. Any canonicalization plan must build migration readers first.

preserved_wire_contract.protocol: local persisted artifacts and in-process typed symbols, not a network protocol
preserved_wire_contract.encoding: JSON, MessagePack, and Bincode legacy config, selected by SerializationFormat, plus a Custom discriminant for downstream codecs
preserved_wire_contract.signal_paths_note: Typed symbols begin with a four-byte TSYM magic in a 27-byte header whose format byte is 1 for MessagePack, 2 for Bincode, 3 for JSON and 255 for Custom; an unknown byte is rejected. Trace files begin with the eleven-byte magic ASUPERTRACE, then a u16 container version, then flags and a compression byte.
preserved_wire_contract.schema_versioning: Five independent version surfaces exist and are preserved: the typed-symbol header version, the trace container version with a forward-rejecting check, the replay schema version with exact-equality matching, the crash-pack current version together with its minimum supported floor, and the per-type name, version and schema hash in TypeRegistry.
preserved_wire_contract.bincode_config_pin: bincode is the bincode-next package aliased to the name bincode, and every call site uses config::legacy(). Both the alias and the legacy pin are part of the persisted contract.

preserved_config_semantics.name: format_selection
preserved_config_semantics.surface: SerializationFormat and the TypedEncoder / TypedDecoder constructors
preserved_config_semantics.contract: All four discriminants remain selectable, and their header byte values remain 1, 2, 3 and 255. Removing, renumbering or reordering is a breaking change to both the API and stored bytes.

preserved_config_semantics.name: custom_codec_injection
preserved_config_semantics.contract: Downstream codecs can be supplied for any discriminant including Custom. This extension point may not be removed or narrowed to a fixed set.

preserved_config_semantics.name: owned_codec_error_surface
preserved_config_semantics.contract: Codec failures are reported as owned variants carrying a reason string rather than by exposing the upstream error type. Size overflow is a distinct variant carrying both the size and the maximum, and an unknown format byte is its own variant.

preserved_config_semantics.name: trace_version_policy
preserved_config_semantics.surface: TRACE_FILE_VERSION check and TraceMetadata compatibility check
preserved_config_semantics.contract: The container version is forward-rejecting and backward-accepting; the embedded replay schema version is exact-equality. That asymmetry is deliberate and must be preserved or deliberately changed with evidence, not drifted into.

preserved_config_semantics.name: crashpack_compatibility_floor
preserved_config_semantics.surface: CrashPackManifest validation against the current and minimum supported schema versions
preserved_config_semantics.contract: Validation enforces a closed supported range. The floor may only rise with a documented migration story.

preserved_config_semantics.name: trace_resource_bounds
preserved_config_semantics.contract: Untrusted trace input is bounded on metadata length, event length, compressed chunk length and preallocation count. Bounds may tighten only with evidence that the existing corpus still loads.

preserved_config_semantics.name: compression_optionality
preserved_config_semantics.contract: Compression is signalled in the header. Uncompressed trace files remain readable regardless of the trace-compression feature.

preserved_config_semantics.name: snapshot_determinism
preserved_config_semantics.surface: bincode legacy config in distributed snapshots
preserved_config_semantics.contract: Vector-clock encoding is deterministic for a given clock. Changing the config or encoder changes the bytes and breaks interchange.

preserved_config_semantics.name: lab_snapshot_hash_stability
preserved_config_semantics.contract: The integrity hash is computed over JSON output, so the JSON encoder is part of the hash contract. Changing it invalidates stored hashes even though no file format changed.

preserved_config_semantics.name: type_versioning
preserved_config_semantics.contract: Each registered type carries a stable name, an explicit version and a schema hash. These identify artifacts across versions and may not be dropped from the container.

known_gaps.summary: The capability registry records source_owners for CAP-SERDE-GENERIC as src/encoding.rs and src/decoding.rs. Both are RaptorQ erasure-coding pipelines and contain zero serde, rmp, bincode or serde_json tokens. The real owner, src/types/typed_symbol.rs, is not named. The root cause is visible in api_surface_snapshot.selectors, which map the module prefixes encoding:: and decoding:: to CAP-SERDE-GENERIC, apparently by matching the words encoding and decoding to serialization, while the types:: prefix is mapped to API topology instead.
known_gaps.consequence: The entire generic Serde surface is attributed to the erasure codec and the real codec is attributed to API topology. This is the third confirmed wrong source_owners row and the first with an identified mechanism, which makes every row suspect until audited.

known_gaps.summary: CAP-PERSISTED-TRACE-SNAPSHOT names src/trace/mod.rs as a source owner, but that file is a pure module facade with no serialization code. The real owners are src/trace/file.rs, replay.rs, crashpack.rs, event.rs, compat.rs, streaming.rs and integrity.rs. Neither src/lab/snapshot_restore.rs nor src/distributed/snapshot.rs is named anywhere, despite the capability title mentioning snapshots and despite the latter being the only production bincode user outside typed_symbol.rs.
known_gaps.consequence: A baseline built from that row would miss the entire trace file implementation, both snapshot surfaces, and the crash-pack format. The same facade-instead-of-implementation error also affects CAP-TRACE-LZ4, whose source_owners names src/trace/mod.rs while every LZ4 call is in src/trace/file.rs.

known_gaps.summary: There is no byte-level golden for the Bincode or MessagePack paths anywhere in the repository. The three format tests assert round-trip only, and the single frozen serialization golden covers JSON.
known_gaps.consequence: A silent change in either binary encoder would not be caught by any existing test, even though both encode persisted artifacts. This is the largest evidence hole behind the capability's BASELINE_PLANNED state.

known_gaps.summary: The persisted trace error surface exposes the MessagePack crate directly: ReplayTrace::to_bytes returns a Result whose error type is rmp_serde::encode::Error, ReplayTraceError holds a #[from] rmp_serde::decode::Error variant and is re-exported at asupersync::trace, and TraceFileError has public From impls naming both rmp error types.
known_gaps.consequence: Unlike the typed-symbol codec, which fully owns its errors, the persisted trace path cannot swap encoders without a breaking public API change.

known_gaps.summary: No migration reader exists for any persisted artifact. Trace containers reject a newer version, replay metadata requires exact version equality, and crash packs enforce a closed range, but nothing converts an older artifact into a newer or canonical form.
known_gaps.consequence: Any future canonicalization must build migration and rollback tooling first, which is why the persisted capability is already BLOCKED_PENDING_EVIDENCE.

known_gaps.summary: bincode is the bincode-next package aliased to the name bincode, and every call site pins bincode::config::legacy(). Neither the alias nor the legacy pin is recorded as a compatibility contract outside the call sites themselves.
known_gaps.consequence: A well-meaning upgrade to the default or standard config would silently change persisted snapshot and typed-symbol bytes.

known_gaps.summary: The lab RestorableSnapshot integrity hash is computed by hashing serde_json output, so the JSON encoder participates in hash stability even though no file format exists there.
known_gaps.consequence: Changing or replacing the JSON encoder silently changes every content hash and invalidates verify_integrity for stored hashes, a failure mode no format-compatibility test would catch.

known_gaps.summary: artifacts/api_surface_map_v1.json contains no codec symbols at all: none of SerdeCodec, SerializationFormat, the two codec traits, TypedSymbol, TypedEncoder, TypedDecoder or TypeRegistry appears. The encoding:: and decoding:: entries it does carry are RaptorQ types.
known_gaps.consequence: The public generic codec surface is invisible to the API drift-detection contract, so a narrowing change there would not be flagged. Correcting it requires adding symbols, and the capability registry pins that map by semantic hash, so it must be done by the map's owner rather than from this ADR.

known_gaps.summary: artifacts/dependency_safety_taxonomy_v1.json still carries the superseded removal framing, describing purpose-built schemas as replacing the public Bincode and MessagePack variants and asserting that the SerdeCodec ADR names the removal of arbitrary Serialize.
known_gaps.consequence: That artifact now contradicts this ADR and the capability registry's KEEP_UNTIL_PARITY disposition. It must be amended by its owner before it is cited as guidance.

security_invariants: Untrusted persisted input is bounded on metadata length, event length, compressed chunk length and preallocation count before any allocation is sized from it.
A trace container whose version exceeds the supported version, or a crash pack outside the supported range, is rejected explicitly rather than parsed optimistically.
An unknown typed-symbol format byte is rejected with a dedicated error rather than defaulted.
Crash-pack persistence requires an explicit writer capability; there are no ambient filesystem writes, and writes are atomic through temp file and rename.
Deserialization of downstream types produces values only and cannot grant ambient authority.
Content hashing stays available so tampering is detectable independently of the encoder.
cancellation_invariants: A partially written trace file is detectable through the header and length framing rather than truncating into a valid-looking file.
Crash-pack writes publish only on rename, so a cancelled write never appears as a complete artifact.
Encode and decode are synchronous pure transformations, so cancelling a surrounding task cannot leave a codec half-applied.
Streaming trace writers release their buffers on drop.

platform_cells.note: The registry scopes CAP-SERDE-GENERIC to the default feature set on all supported platforms, and all four format crates are unconditional.
The persisted trace container and the trace-inspection CLI are native-facing, since the cli feature is native-only.

TypedEncoder::with_serializer and TypedDecoder::with_deserializer for custom codec injection

pinned_crate_versions.bincode: package bincode-next 3.1.1 with the serde feature, always used with config::legacy() (non-optional)

external_ecosystem_integration.no_reexport_note: No format crate is re-exported, and the typed-symbol errors deliberately stringify upstream failures rather than wrapping them, so the codec itself could swap backends without an API break. The persisted trace error surface is the exception and is recorded as SER-GAP-04.
external_ecosystem_integration.runtime_seam_is_clean: The typed-symbol container, its header, TypeRegistry versioning and the two codec traits are all owned. The dependency is confined to the three encoders behind the dispatch, the persisted trace error conversions, and the lab snapshot hash input.
external_ecosystem_integration.removal_precondition: An owned implementation must cover the full Serde data model, reproduce the accepted bytes for existing persisted artifacts including the bincode legacy dialect, match error and resource semantics, and offer comparable usability, validated against synthesized arbitrary-type consumers, the persisted corpus, a malformed corpus and working migration readers. Byte goldens for Bincode and MessagePack must exist first, since SER-GAP-03 shows nothing would currently detect a divergence. Until then: KEEP for the generic formats and BLOCKED_PENDING_EVIDENCE for the persisted artifacts.

user_journeys.description: Downstream defines its own Serialize and DeserializeOwned type and round-trips it through SerdeCodec in each of the three real formats. Executed today by the standalone consumer fixture, including a boundary fixture with extreme integers, an empty-string map key, non-ASCII text and raw bytes.
Downstream implements the public Serializer and Deserializer traits, injects them through with_serializer and with_deserializer, and owns the Custom discriminant.
A truncated payload produces an owned deserialization error, the Custom discriminant is rejected by SerdeCodec, and the codec remains usable afterwards. Asserted today by the consumer fixture.
A consumer registers a type with a name and version, encodes a typed symbol, and later detects a type or version mismatch rather than misreading the payload.
An operator captures a trace to disk and replays it later through the CLI, in both compressed and uncompressed form, relying on the container magic and version.
An artifact written by an earlier build still loads. This is the journey the Rev-3 proposal would have broken, because trace payloads are MessagePack and snapshot vector clocks are Bincode.
Two nodes exchange snapshots whose vector clocks encode deterministically to identical bytes for identical clocks.

migration_policy.additive_only: New owned artifact schemas and any canonical encoding are added alongside the existing formats. No accepted persisted artifact may become unreadable and no format discriminant may be removed or renumbered.
migration_policy.coexistence: The generic codec keeps all four discriminants indefinitely. Owned schemas may take over new artifact writes only once a reader for the existing corpus exists.
migration_policy.sequencing: Byte goldens for Bincode and MessagePack come first, then a persisted corpus, then migration readers. Only then can canonicalization change what is written. The persisted capability stays BLOCKED_PENDING_EVIDENCE until then.
migration_policy.docs_obligation: Any change to the frozen surface updates this artifact, docs/dependency_api_adr_registry.md, and docs/adr/dep_plan_adr_001_serde_generic_formats.md in the same commit.

rollback_policy.trigger: Any previously written trace file, crash pack or snapshot that stops loading, any removed or renumbered format discriminant, any loss of the custom codec injection points, any change to the bincode legacy config or to a container magic or version, any coarsened codec error, any changed lab snapshot content hash, or any tightened resource bound that rejects an artifact in the existing corpus.
rollback_policy.action: Revert to the frozen surface recorded here. Because the decision is additive coexistence, rollback removes the new owned schema path rather than restoring a deleted format.
rollback_policy.verification: Re-run the focused ADR contract and the five scenario IDs owned by the two capabilities, and re-read the persisted corpus end to end.

unit: empty, boundary and maximum sizes, malformed bytes, truncation, the value-too-large path with its size and maximum, and the unknown-format-byte path
unit: type and version mismatch detection through TypeRegistry including schema-hash disagreement
golden: byte-level goldens for the Bincode and MessagePack paths, which SER-GAP-03 records as entirely absent today
property: round-trip idempotence over generated downstream types in each format
differential: byte stability for the bincode legacy dialect and for MessagePack across crate versions
fuzz: malformed persisted input bounded by the trace and snapshot limits with no panic

E2E: trace capture, CLI replay and artifact rollback
evidence.note: Naming these owners does not assert they have run. The persisted capability is BLOCKED_PENDING_EVIDENCE, so no cutover claim can rest on it today. The serialization-golden harnesses do not currently cover the codec and may not be cited for it.

cutover.note: This ADR authorizes no dependency exit. The two capabilities deliberately carry different postures: the generic formats keep the incumbent, while the persisted artifacts may be replaced only on proven parity and are currently blocked.

adrs.no_claim_boundary: This ADR is a frozen decision and public-surface inventory only. It does not prove that the planned evidence has run, that the persisted corpus still loads, that byte stability holds across format-crate versions, that an owned serializer could cover the Serde data model, that migration readers are feasible, that performance is unchanged, or that any format dependency may be removed. It also does not certify the capability registry's source-owner rows, the api surface map, or the dependency safety taxonomy, which SER-GAP-01, SER-GAP-02, SER-GAP-08 and SER-GAP-09 record as incorrect or superseded for these capabilities.

adrs.title: Preserve arbitrary downstream Protobuf messages and ergonomic authoring
adrs.decision_summary: `prost` stays as the public authoring and codec boundary. `ProstCodec<T, U>` is an unrestricted generic surface: the struct carries no bounds at all, and the `Codec` impl accepts any `T: prost::Message + Send + 'static` and `U: prost::Message + Default + Send + 'static`, so any downstream crate can plug in its own derived or generated message type. The claim-time source read produced the argument that settles this. The finite message sets that the Rev-3 plan proposed to hand-write in exchange for dropping prost — gRPC health and reflection — are ALREADY prost-free today, and the only closed prost message set in the crate, `otlp_logs_proto`, is module-private. So prost buys exactly one thing: the arbitrary downstream generic surface. Trading it for a finite set would surrender the entire capability while gaining nothing that is not already owned. Owning further finite internal message sets is permitted and already happens; it is not a path to removing prost.

alternatives_considered.option: Replace `ProstCodec` with an owned `ProtoMessage` trait over a finite hand-written message set, per the Rev-3 plan.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It would delete `ProstCodec<T, U>`, `SymmetricProstCodec<T>`, and both prost-typed `ProtobufError` variants, and would break the executable downstream journey in tests/fixtures/dependency-capability-baseline-consumer plus six conformance tests and eight fuzz targets. The bead states outright that a finite hand-written set removes functionality and is forbidden, and the capability registry's no-claim boundary says finite in-repo schemas cannot replace arbitrary downstream Protobuf capability.

alternatives_considered.option: Justify the finite set by pointing at gRPC health, reflection, and status-details as the messages that matter.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Those surfaces contain zero prost references today. src/grpc/health.rs and src/grpc/reflection.rs are already hand-written and prost-free, so this alternative describes work that is already done and would not remove the dependency. It mistakes the internal message sets for the capability.

alternatives_considered.option: Own a `ProtoMessage` trait plus a production-quality derive macro and codegen, matching prost's ergonomics.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Not rejected in principle, but it is a very large piece of work that must clear a high bar before it can be evaluated: arbitrary downstream compile and runtime fixtures, cross-language Protobuf and gRPC interop, malformed and resource-limit behavior, fuzzing, and rollback. Manual trait implementation alone is explicitly not equivalent ergonomics. Until that exists and passes, KEEP.

alternatives_considered.option: Narrow the public surface to `SymmetricProstCodec<T>` only, since it is the common case.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Asymmetric request and response types are the normal gRPC shape, and the doc example itself uses `ProstCodec<HelloRequest, HelloResponse>`. Collapsing the two parameters is generic-API narrowing.

alternatives_considered.option: Make `prost` optional behind a feature so it leaves the default graph.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: `prost = "0.14"` is currently a plain non-optional dependency, so protobuf support is unconditional on native targets. Gating it would remove capability from every consumer who does not opt in, which is narrowing by another name. If the marginal graph cost is the concern, that is a measurement question for the marginal ledger, not a licence to gate a shipped public API.

preserved_public_symbols.note: The blessed short path. `pub mod grpc` is platform-gated to non-wasm32 but carries no feature gate, so this is default-feature public API.

`SymmetricProstCodec<T>` is NOT re-exported at `asupersync::grpc` and is reachable only by this long path; it is public API regardless. `ProstCodec::new`, `Default`, and `Clone` are all implemented without bounds, so a codec value can be constructed for any pair of types.
The generic seam `ProstCodec` implements. Client and server are generic over `Codec`, which is what makes a downstream `ProstCodec<Req, Resp>` usable end to end.
`GrpcClient<C>` is generic over `Codec`, defaulting to `IdentityCodec`.
Server-side `framed_codec` is generic over `Codec` on the same seam.
Streaming must keep working with the generic codec, not only with unary calls; the bead requires generic codec use in both.
Service description surface downstream authors implement alongside their own messages.
Status mapping is part of the interop contract; codec errors surface through it.
Already hand-written and prost-free. Frozen here as evidence that the finite internal message sets do not require prost, which is the core of this ADR's argument.
Also already prost-free.

preserved_feature_flags.name: default
preserved_feature_flags.effect: The protobuf surface is NOT behind any feature. `prost` is a plain non-optional dependency, so `ProstCodec` and the gRPC stack are available in a default build on non-wasm32 targets. This row exists to pin that fact: making protobuf feature-gated would be capability narrowing.
preserved_feature_flags.no_tokio_guarantee: prost's only dependencies are bytes and prost-derive; it introduces no tokio edge.

preserved_feature_flags.name: compression
preserved_feature_flags.effect: Gates the gzip frame compressor and decompressor used with `FramedCodec` around `ProstCodec`, and the gzip parity conformance coverage.

preserved_feature_flags.name: fuzz
preserved_feature_flags.effect: Enables the arbitrary-derive support used by the eight `ProstCodec` fuzz targets, and separately the quarantined OTLP proto helpers.
preserved_feature_flags.no_tokio_guarantee: Explicitly excluded from the no-Tokio production guarantee via the opentelemetry-proto edge; that carve-out is documented by DEP-ADR-003.

preserved_surfaces.note: The whole capability. Unrestricted in the type parameters; the size limit is enforced before encode via encoded_len and before decode, so oversized messages are rejected without allocating.
Already owned and prost-free. Any owned protobuf implementation would plug in here rather than replacing this.
Decisive for this ADR: the finite sets the Rev-3 plan wanted to hand-write in exchange for dropping prost already exist without it.

preserved_surfaces.wire_encoder: hand-rolled prost derives in a module-private message set
preserved_surfaces.note: The only closed prost message set in the crate. It is module-private and does not exercise the generic codec, so it is not evidence about the generic capability. Owned by DEP-ADR-003.

There is no src/codec/proto.rs and no owned ProtoMessage trait. The varint helpers in src/grpc/protobuf.rs are cfg(test) differential-oracle code, not reusable production code, and must not be cited as a partial implementation.

Neither prost-build nor prost-types is a dependency and there is no build-script codegen. Downstream authors rely on prost's derive macro, which is exactly the ergonomics an owned replacement would have to reproduce.

preserved_wire_contract.encoding: Protocol Buffers as implemented by prost 0.14
preserved_wire_contract.signal_paths_note: Length-prefixed message framing is one compression byte followed by a big-endian u32 length, then the encoded message. Byte parity with other gRPC implementations is an explicit conformance claim in the repository's own test suite.
preserved_wire_contract.http_status_semantics: gRPC status codes via the owned Code and Status types
preserved_wire_contract.collector_interop: Cross-language Protobuf and gRPC interoperability with other implementations is part of the capability, not an optional extra.
preserved_wire_contract.accepted_data_model: All Protobuf scalar and wire types, packed fields, maps, oneofs, repeated and nested messages, enums, and unknown-field preservation, as accepted by prost 0.14. The downstream fixture exercises uint64, repeated string, a string-to-int64 map, and a two-variant oneof.

preserved_config_semantics.name: max_message_size
preserved_config_semantics.contract: Defaults to DEFAULT_MAX_MESSAGE_SIZE, 4 MiB. Enforced before encoding using the computed encoded length and before decoding, so an oversized message is rejected without allocating it.

preserved_config_semantics.name: size_error_reporting
preserved_config_semantics.contract: Carries both the actual size and the configured limit. Reducing this to an opaque error is a diagnostic regression.

preserved_config_semantics.name: error_variant_distinctness
preserved_config_semantics.contract: Encode failure, decode failure, and size-limit failure stay three distinct variants. The encode and decode variants currently wrap prost's own error types, which is itself part of the frozen surface.

preserved_config_semantics.name: varint_strictness
preserved_config_semantics.contract: A ten-byte varint encoding u64::MAX is accepted; a ten-byte varint with bits above u64, an eleven-byte varint, and an unterminated ten-byte varint are all rejected. The size limit is checked before decoding begins.

preserved_config_semantics.name: unknown_field_policy
preserved_config_semantics.contract: Whatever prost 0.14 does for unknown fields is the accepted behavior, and schema evolution depends on it. Any owned replacement must match it exactly, not approximately.

preserved_config_semantics.name: streaming_use
preserved_config_semantics.surface: FramedCodec around ProstCodec in client and server streaming
preserved_config_semantics.contract: Message ordering is preserved across long streams; the repository pins a hundred-message server-streaming ordering case.

preserved_config_semantics.name: compression_interop
preserved_config_semantics.contract: gzip and identity frames must decode to an identical message tree, with no double decoding.

known_gaps.summary: The capability registry records source_owners for CAP-PROTOBUF-GENERIC as src/grpc/mod.rs and src/encoding.rs. src/encoding.rs is the RaptorQ FEC encoding pipeline and contains zero occurrences of prost or protobuf, and src/grpc/protobuf.rs, which actually defines ProstCodec and ProtobufError, is not named at all.
known_gaps.consequence: Inventory or baseline work that trusts that row will read an unrelated FEC module and miss the file that owns the capability. This is the second confirmed instance of the same defect class in the registry.

known_gaps.summary: Two files under src/ exercise ProstCodec with downstream-style messages over real HTTP/2 gRPC streaming, but neither is declared as a module anywhere, so neither is ever compiled.
known_gaps.consequence: They look like the richest end-to-end downstream-message journeys in the tree but provide zero coverage. They may not be counted as evidence while they remain undeclared.

known_gaps.summary: There is no gRPC or protobuf example under examples/, and the module-level doc example showing a downstream author defining messages and building a ProstCodec is inside an ignore fence, so it is never compiled.
known_gaps.consequence: The primary authoring journey this ADR protects has no executed demonstration outside the standalone consumer fixture.

known_gaps.summary: ProtobufError wraps prost's own encode and decode error types in two of its three variants, so the public error surface is not prost-free.
known_gaps.consequence: Any replacement changes the public error type, not merely the internal codec. That cost belongs in the replacement's parity budget and must not be discovered late.

known_gaps.summary: ProstCodec does not override the Codec trait's set_max_encode_message_size or set_max_decode_message_size, whose default bodies are no-ops, so runtime limit renegotiation never reaches it. Only construction-time with_max_size has effect.
known_gaps.consequence: An operator or peer-negotiated message-size change does not apply to a ProstCodec. This is current behavior and is frozen as such, but it is a real limitation rather than a designed guarantee.

known_gaps.summary: The capability baseline records CAP-PROTOBUF-GENERIC as EXECUTABLE_PARTIAL_BLOCKING: the positive, empty and boundary, malformed and error, and resource-limit cases have evidence, but cancellation cleanup is blocked on an owner and recovery is blocked externally.
known_gaps.consequence: Cancellation and recovery behavior for the generic codec is unproven, so a cutover cannot claim lifecycle parity today.

security_invariants: Untrusted wire input stays bounded: the size limit is enforced before decode, and malformed varints, wire types, lengths, depths, and truncation are rejected rather than absorbed.
The decode path allocates only after the size check passes, so an oversized declared length cannot drive allocation.
The unknown-field policy is explicit and inherited from prost; it may not silently change under a replacement.
The codec kernel stays strictly safe: no unsafe code is introduced on the protobuf path.
cancellation_invariants: Partial frames remain owned by the connection and are not leaked on cancellation.
Stream cancellation releases buffers and any reservations held by the framed codec.
These are stated obligations, not proven ones; PB-GAP-06 records that the cancellation and recovery cases are currently blocked.

platform_cells.note: The registry scopes CAP-PROTOBUF-GENERIC to all supported platforms and to the default feature set.
`pub mod grpc` is gated to non-wasm32, so the protobuf and gRPC surface is absent on wasm32 by construction. That exclusion is pre-existing and is not a loss introduced here.

entry_points: asupersync::grpc::ProstCodec as a codec over any downstream prost::Message
asupersync::grpc::protobuf::SymmetricProstCodec for same-type request and response
prost's own derive macro, used by downstream crates to author message types
external_ecosystem_integration.accepted_providers: Any type implementing prost::Message, whether hand-derived downstream or produced by prost-build in the consumer's own build script.
external_ecosystem_integration.no_reexport_note: asupersync does not re-export prost, so downstream consumers depend on it directly and must resolve to a compatible version. The standalone consumer fixture pins prost to exactly 0.14.4 and asserts that pin, which makes a prost major bump a downstream-visible break requiring its own evidence.
external_ecosystem_integration.runtime_seam_is_clean: The Codec trait, the framing layer, and the client and server seams are all owned and prost-free. The dependency is confined to the message type bound and the two wrapped error variants.
external_ecosystem_integration.removal_precondition: An owned replacement must provide an authoring experience at least as usable as prost's derive, accept arbitrary downstream schemas, match the full accepted data model including maps, oneofs, packed fields and unknown-field evolution, preserve the error surface or justify changing it, and pass arbitrary-downstream compile and runtime fixtures, cross-language Protobuf and gRPC interop, malformed and resource tests, fuzzing, and rollback. Manual trait implementation alone does not qualify as equivalent ergonomics unless the owner explicitly finds it better after consumer trials. Until then: KEEP.

user_journeys.description: Downstream author derives their own prost message with scalars, repeated fields, a map, and a oneof, builds a ProstCodec over it, and round-trips it. This is executed today by the standalone consumer fixture, which deliberately builds without test-internals.
Author uses distinct request and response types through ProstCodec<Req, Resp> in a unary gRPC call, the shape the module documentation itself demonstrates.
Author uses the generic codec for client, server, and bidirectional streaming, relying on preserved message ordering across long streams.
Operator sets a message size limit and receives a MessageTooLarge error naming both the actual size and the limit, rather than an opaque failure.
Messages encoded by asupersync are consumed by a non-Rust gRPC implementation and vice versa, relying on exact wire-byte compatibility.
Author enables gzip framing and gets an identical decoded message tree to the identity path.

api_surface_delta.rationale: This ADR makes no source change. Every frozen symbol lives under `asupersync::grpc`, not at the crate root, and the capability registry pins the api surface map by semantic hash.

supersedes.stale_text: owned ProtoMessage trait over a finite message set; drop the public arbitrary-prost::Message surface
supersedes.resolution: Rejected by the no-loss gate. Dropping the arbitrary surface is precisely the functionality removal this ADR exists to prevent.

supersedes.stale_text: Owned ProtoMessage trait plus hand-written finite message set (gRPC health/reflection/status-details; OTLP export subset) replaces prost
supersedes.resolution: The premise does not hold. The gRPC health and reflection message sets are already hand-written and prost-free, and the OTLP subset is a module-private set owned by DEP-ADR-003. Building those does not remove prost, because prost is required only for the arbitrary downstream generic surface.

supersedes.stale_text: OWN (SAFE) ... owned ProtoMessage trait + finite hand-written message types replace the public generic ProstCodec
supersedes.resolution: Disposition is KEEP_UNTIL_PARITY, not OWN. The row's dependent claim that the OpenTelemetry replacement depends on the prost replacement is also unnecessary: an owned OTLP message set can be written with prost derives exactly as otlp_logs_proto already is.

migration_policy.additive_only: Owning further finite internal message sets is permitted and already happens. Doing so adds capability; it does not subtract the generic surface and is not a step toward removing prost.
migration_policy.coexistence: prost remains the public authoring and codec boundary. An owned protobuf implementation, if ever built, would plug into the existing Codec seam alongside ProstCodec rather than replacing it, until parity is proven.
migration_policy.sequencing: The baseline corpus for the full accepted data model must exist before any replacement is evaluable, and the currently blocked cancellation and recovery cases must be unblocked before lifecycle parity can be claimed.
migration_policy.docs_obligation: Any change to the frozen surface updates this artifact, docs/dependency_api_adr_registry.md, and docs/adr/dep_plan_adr_002_protobuf_generic.md in the same commit.

rollback_policy.trigger: Any downstream crate that can no longer author or use its own message type, any narrowing of the accepted data model, any loss of a ProtobufError variant or of the size and limit detail, any wire-byte divergence from other gRPC implementations, any streaming ordering change, or any prost major bump that breaks the pinned consumer fixture.
rollback_policy.action: Revert to the frozen surface recorded here. Because the decision is KEEP, rollback means abandoning the replacement attempt rather than restoring a deleted capability.
rollback_policy.verification: Re-run the focused ADR contract, the six gRPC codec conformance tests, the eight ProstCodec fuzz targets, and the standalone downstream consumer fixture before declaring the rollback complete.

required_evidence_classes: unit: full accepted data model including scalars, repeated, packed, maps, enums, oneofs, nested messages, and unknown-field evolution
unit: empty message, boundary and maximum sizes, malformed varints, wrong wire types, truncation, and recursion depth
unit: cancellation, race, shutdown, leak, and quiescence behavior for the framed codec, which PB-GAP-06 records as currently blocked
property: round-trip idempotence over generated message trees
differential: byte-for-byte agreement with prost for encode and decode, and length-prefixed framing parity with other gRPC implementations
fuzz: the existing ProstCodec fuzz targets covering decode, huge messages, framing, and malformed varint overflow
downstream-consumer: a standalone crate outside the workspace authoring its own message with map and oneof fields, compiled without test-internals, with its prost version pinned
cross-language E2E: interoperability with a non-Rust gRPC implementation in both directions
streaming E2E: ordering preserved across long client, server, and bidirectional streams
evidence.note: Naming these owners does not assert they have run. The two undeclared files recorded in PB-GAP-02 and the ignore-fenced doc example in PB-GAP-03 may not be counted toward any of these classes.

cutover.note: This ADR authorizes no dependency exit. prost remains a non-optional production dependency. Phase-5 protobuf children inherit the KEEP and must not proceed on the assumption that the generic surface is being retired.

adrs.no_claim_boundary: This ADR is a frozen decision and public-surface inventory only. It does not prove that the planned evidence has run, that cross-language interoperability has been demonstrated, that cancellation and recovery behavior is correct, that an owned protobuf implementation could reach ergonomic or wire parity, that performance is unchanged, or that prost may be removed. It also does not certify the capability registry's source-owner rows, which PB-GAP-01 records as incorrect for this capability.

adrs.title: Preserve OTLP metrics + traces + logs and external SDK/provider/collector interoperability
adrs.decision_summary: Keep both telemetry tiers that ship today, because they are not redundant: they cover different signals. Tier 1 is the owned, hand-rolled OTLP surface, which reaches the wire in production for the logs signal only. Tier 2 is the external OpenTelemetry ecosystem bridge, and for the metrics and traces signals it is the only production export path that exists. The three `OtelMetrics` constructors each take an `opentelemetry::metrics::Meter` supplied by the embedder, and the re-exported `SpanStorage` type materializes spans through an embedder-supplied `opentelemetry::trace::BoxedTracer`. Deleting the `opentelemetry` and `opentelemetry_sdk` dependencies would therefore not merely remove an optional integration; it would leave asupersync with no production metrics or traces export at all. The dependencies are KEEP_UNTIL_PARITY and the capability stays KEEP_INCUMBENT.

alternatives_considered.option: Remove `opentelemetry` and `opentelemetry_sdk`; ship only the owned OTLP/HTTP exporters.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The owned OTLP request builders for the metrics and traces signals live in `observability::otel::otlp_request_builder`, which is gated `#[cfg(all(any(test, feature = "fuzz"), feature = "metrics", feature = "tracing-integration"))]`. They are unreachable in any production build. Removing the ecosystem crates would delete the only production metrics and traces export path and also delete `OtelMetrics::new`, the sole integration point for downstream code that already owns a `MeterProvider`. That is compound capability loss.

alternatives_considered.option: Keep the OTLP wire path for two of the three signals and drop the third.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: `otlp-logs-omission` is a named historical loss fixture in the capability registry. The logs signal is in fact the single best-supported one: `LogsSnapshot::to_otlp_protobuf` and the `otlp_logs_proto` prost message set are ungated inside the `metrics`-gated module, so they encode and send in production today. Dropping it would remove the only owned end-to-end OTLP wire path in the crate.

alternatives_considered.option: Route the owned trace pipeline through the ecosystem crates and delete `otlp_trace_exporter`.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: `observability::otlp_trace_exporter` is ungated: its types, bounded queue, head-based sampling, and brownout policy are available at default features with no `opentelemetry` dependency. Folding it into the ecosystem crates would make that surface feature-gated and would add a dependency edge to the default production graph.

alternatives_considered.option: Promote `otlp_request_builder` out of its test/fuzz gate so metrics and traces get an owned production wire path.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It depends on `opentelemetry-proto`, which is deliberately quarantined behind `fuzz` because its `gen-tonic-messages` feature pulls `tonic` and therefore `tokio`. Promoting it as written would put a tokio edge in the metrics production graph and break the no-Tokio guarantee. Closing this gap requires an owned prost message set in the style of `otlp_logs_proto`, which is real implementation work owned by asupersync-5z2scg.2, not an ADR decision.

alternatives_considered.option: Enable the `logs` feature on the `opentelemetry`/`opentelemetry_sdk` crates to back the logs signal.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The production `metrics` feature deliberately pins both crates to `default-features = false, features = ["metrics", "trace"]`. Widening that set grows the production graph for a signal that already has a working owned implementation. Deferred, not rejected on principle.

preserved_public_symbols.note: Dependency-free in-process metrics registry and the runtime's `MetricsProvider` seam. Available with no Cargo features enabled and entirely free of OpenTelemetry types.
Owned in-process OTLP trace pipeline. Ungated: available at default features with no `opentelemetry` dependency.

Ungated re-export, but `SpanStorage` methods take and return `opentelemetry::Context`, `BoxedTracer`, `BoxedSpan`, `Status`, and `Value`. This is a hard ecosystem coupling on a type reachable at default features.
W3C Trace Context and Baggage propagation, implemented without any OpenTelemetry crate dependency.
Curated `metrics`-gated re-export set from `observability::otel`.

`pub mod otel` is public, so every `pub` item is reachable API even when it is absent from the curated re-export list. `OtlpHttpExporter` and `PrivacyConfig` in particular are reachable only by the long path, and `PrivacyConfig` already has an external-consumer smoke fixture under tests/fixtures/dependency-capability-baseline-consumer.

preserved_feature_flags.name: metrics
preserved_feature_flags.effect: Enables `observability::otel` (owned OTLP/HTTP logs exporter, the shared `OtlpHttpExporter` transport, the external `Meter` bridge, privacy/redaction, and cardinality control) plus `observability::histogram_conformance`. `regex` is required by the PII redaction engine.
preserved_feature_flags.no_tokio_guarantee: The `metrics` production graph must have no normal-edge dependency on tokio. Proof lane `metrics-production-tokio-tree`: `cargo tree -e normal -p asupersync --features metrics -i tokio` must print `warning: nothing to print.`

preserved_feature_flags.name: tracing-integration
preserved_feature_flags.effect: Enables the real `observability::otel::span_semantics` module; without it a stub is compiled instead. Also required, together with `test`/`fuzz`, to reach `otlp_request_builder`.
preserved_feature_flags.no_tokio_guarantee: Not an OTLP transport dependency; listed because the capability registry maps it to CAP-OTLP-ECOSYSTEM.

preserved_feature_flags.name: compression
preserved_feature_flags.effect: Enables gzip request-body compression in `OtlpHttpExporter`. Without it, calling `with_compression(true)` is a hard error rather than a silent downgrade.

preserved_feature_flags.name: fuzz
preserved_feature_flags.effect: Enables `opentelemetry-proto` with `gen-tonic-messages`, `trace`, `metrics`, and `logs`, which is what makes `otlp_request_builder` reachable for conformance, golden, and fuzz helpers.
preserved_feature_flags.no_tokio_guarantee: Explicitly EXCLUDED from the no-Tokio production guarantee. Proof lane `fuzz-tokio-quarantine-tree` expects the `opentelemetry-proto` -> `tonic`/`tonic-prost` -> `tokio` path and treats it as an accepted, documented quarantine edge.

preserved_surfaces.wire_encoder: LogsSnapshot::to_otlp_protobuf via the ungated internal `otlp_logs_proto` prost message set
preserved_surfaces.note: The only signal with a complete owned production path from snapshot to wire. Implemented WITHOUT the ecosystem crates' logs feature. `otlp-logs-omission` is a named historical loss fixture; this signal may not be dropped.

preserved_surfaces.wire_encoder: none in production; `otlp_request_builder::metrics_request_from_snapshot` is gated to test/fuzz
preserved_surfaces.transport: the embedder's own opentelemetry_sdk reader and exporter
preserved_surfaces.note: `OtelMetrics` records into real `opentelemetry` instruments obtained from a caller-supplied `Meter`. Production metrics therefore leave the process through the embedder's SDK pipeline, not through asupersync. The dependency-free `observability::metrics` registry and its Prometheus exposition text format remain available at default features as a separate, non-OTLP path.

preserved_surfaces.wire_encoder: none in production; `otlp_request_builder::traces_request` is gated to test/fuzz
preserved_surfaces.transport: the embedder's own opentelemetry_sdk tracer for exported spans; the owned pipeline is in-process only
preserved_surfaces.note: The owned trace pipeline ships ungated with bounded queues, head-based sampling, and brownout policy, but the only shipped `TraceExporter` implementation buffers in memory. Spans that actually reach a collector do so through the embedder's SDK via `SpanStorage` and `BoxedTracer`. Tail-based sampling is explicitly and deliberately unsupported, pinned by `otlp_tail_based_sampling_scope`.

`OtelMetrics::new(Meter)`, `OtelMetrics::new_with_resource_detection(Meter, ...)`, and `OtelMetrics::new_with_config(Meter, MetricsConfig)` all accept a `Meter` from ANY downstream `MeterProvider`. This is the whole third-party-ecosystem interop capability and the primary reason the `opentelemetry` dependency is KEEP_UNTIL_PARITY.

preserved_wire_contract.signal_paths_note: The endpoint is caller-supplied verbatim. Asupersync does not append `/v1/logs`, `/v1/metrics`, or `/v1/traces`, and must not begin silently rewriting caller paths.
preserved_wire_contract.temporality: Cumulative only. Hardcoded in the request builders and guarded by a source-text regression test that fails if a Delta path appears without prev-value and reset tracking.
preserved_wire_contract.http_status_semantics: 2xx OK; 408, 429, and 502-504 retryable honoring Retry-After; 405 non-retryable echoing the Allow header; 415 triggers a single uncompressed retry; all other 4xx and 5xx are non-retryable with the batch dropped.
preserved_wire_contract.retry_jitter: Deterministic, not random, so replay stays reproducible.
preserved_wire_contract.collector_interop: Content type, resource and scope attributes, severity mapping, partial-success handling, throttling, and Retry-After parsing must stay collector-compatible.

preserved_config_semantics.name: endpoint
preserved_config_semantics.contract: Caller-supplied full signal URL, used verbatim.

preserved_config_semantics.name: timeout
preserved_config_semantics.contract: Per-attempt timeout, default 10s. Expiry maps to a non-retryable error and the batch is dropped rather than requeued, which is what keeps exporter memory bounded.

preserved_config_semantics.name: retry
preserved_config_semantics.contract: max_retries default 3, initial delay default 100ms, max delay default 30s, exponential doubling clamped to max delay, Retry-After taking precedence when present. There is no retry queue; a single body is held across attempts.

preserved_config_semantics.name: compression
preserved_config_semantics.contract: gzip request bodies, default OFF. The default must not silently change. Requesting compression without the `compression` feature is a hard error, never a silent downgrade.

preserved_config_semantics.name: auth
preserved_config_semantics.contract: Headers are attached to every request. They must be treated as secret material by any redaction, logging, or diagnostics surface.

preserved_config_semantics.name: tls
preserved_config_semantics.contract: Fail-closed. With neither `tls-native-roots` nor `tls-webpki-roots`, the root store is empty and the client build fails. There is no silent system-CA fallback and no HTTPS-to-HTTP downgrade; TLS errors are non-retryable.

preserved_config_semantics.name: resource_attributes
preserved_config_semantics.contract: Three sources with fixed precedence: built-in defaults, then `OTEL_RESOURCE_ATTRIBUTES`, then programmatic attributes. Host-name detection is opt-in.

preserved_config_semantics.name: scope_attributes
preserved_config_semantics.contract: Defaults are the pinned scope name and schema URL; both are overridable per snapshot.

preserved_config_semantics.name: cardinality
preserved_config_semantics.contract: Bounded unique label combinations per metric and bounded distinct metric names, with an explicit overflow strategy of Drop, Aggregate, or Warn and an observable overflow count.

preserved_config_semantics.name: privacy_redaction
preserved_config_semantics.contract: Attribute and label drop lists, a glob allowlist, custom regex patterns, and built-in detectors for email, SSN, Luhn-validated payment cards, and phone numbers. Applies across traces, metrics, and logs. Redaction may only widen, never narrow.

preserved_config_semantics.name: attribute_caps
preserved_config_semantics.contract: 128 attributes and 4096 value bytes, with `dropped_attributes_count` accounting rather than silent truncation.

preserved_config_semantics.name: sampling
preserved_config_semantics.contract: Per-metric sample rates plus a head-based span filter that drops unsampled spans before export. Sampling decisions are deterministic.

preserved_config_semantics.name: load_shedding
preserved_config_semantics.contract: Bounded queues shed with counted drops. The metrics queue drops newest; the trace queue drops oldest to preserve recency. Trace shedding is driven by runtime resource-monitor brownout levels with three actions: export all, drop low priority, retain summary only.

known_gaps.summary: No owned production wire encoder for the metrics and traces signals. `otlp_request_builder` is gated to test and fuzz builds because it depends on the tokio-carrying `opentelemetry-proto`.

adrs.title: Additive canonical JSON while preserving accepted TOML config and YAML scenarios
adrs.decision_summary: TOML runtime/CLI configuration and YAML lab scenarios are operator- and author-facing accepted inputs and stay accepted. Canonical JSON is additive output and an additional accepted input; it never becomes the only accepted form. `toml` and `serde_yaml` remain KEEP_UNTIL_PARITY. The `Scenario` type contains no YAML code, so `serde_yaml` remains at loader and test call sites rather than in a library public signature. `serde_json` is non-optional, and A2 made `Scenario::to_json` a compact, recursively key-ordered canonical encoder for the typed Scenario schema. JSON configuration loading, a shared/config-agnostic canonical encoder, and CLI Scenario JSON input or canonical output remain NOT_SHIPPED. CLI `--json` serializes command results and reports, not Scenario documents.

alternatives_considered.option: Migrate configuration and scenarios to canonical versioned JSON and stop accepting TOML and YAML.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Both are accepted operator and author inputs with a live typed corpus: ten Scenario files under `examples/scenarios/` and three under `frankenlab/examples/scenarios/`, plus a documented `getting_started` journey. `tools/demos/time_travel.yaml` is an adjacent parameter reference rather than the Scenario schema or a benchmark input. Dropping accepted TOML or typed YAML acceptance is direct user-journey loss and the no-loss gate rejects it.

alternatives_considered.option: Keep TOML and YAML, but make canonical JSON the primary on-disk format and demote the others to legacy.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: `Scenario::to_json` now provides compact canonical JSON for the typed Scenario schema, but neither CLI accepts or emits canonical Scenario JSON, no exact 13-file cross-format proof exists, JSON configuration loading is absent, and no shared/config-agnostic canonical encoder exists. Promoting JSON to the primary on-disk format before those journeys and boundaries exist would freeze an aspiration.

alternatives_considered.option: Replace `serde_yaml` with an owned YAML parser now, since it is only used at three call sites.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Call-site count understates the obligation. The accepted grammar is whatever `serde_yaml` 0.9 accepts across the live corpus — anchors, aliases, merge keys, tags, number and Unicode handling, and duplicate-key policy — and none of that is specified anywhere yet. `asupersync-5z2scg.5.1` owns establishing the accepted subset from evidence. Until that exists, an owned parser cannot be shown to preserve the capability.

alternatives_considered.option: Replace `toml` with the existing hand-rolled parser in `src/config.rs`, which already reads a TOML-shaped format.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: `src/config.rs` is not a TOML parser. It makes zero `toml::` calls and hand-splits lines on `=` with `[section]` headers, lowercasing section names and stripping `#` and `//` comments. It accepts a narrower, different grammar with different error semantics. Routing real TOML through it would silently narrow accepted input.

alternatives_considered.option: Add JSON configuration loading in this ADR.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: This bead is decision-only. The decision authorizes JSON config as additive, but the implementation, its precedence semantics, and its round-trip evidence belong to `asupersync-5z2scg.4` and its children.

known_gaps.summary: The capability registry records `source_owners` for CAP-CONFIG-TOML-JSON as src/config.rs and src/bin/asupersync.rs. known_gaps.consequence: The observed subset is pinned, but an owned parser still cannot claim complete parity while current unbounded accepted witness families conflict with finite application limits.

adrs.title: Capability-complete, accessible CLI contract and tracing/config edges
adrs.decision_summary: clap stays as the parser for all four installed binaries. The Rev-3 plan already re-scoped an owned parser to XL after measuring roughly 33.8k lines across six clap-consuming sources with hundreds of derive sites, and this ADR does not overturn that estimate. What it adds is the reason a replacement cannot even be evaluated yet: the CLI contract is currently pinned by source hashes rather than behavior. There is no --help golden anywhere in the repository for any of the four binaries, the help/OsString/accessibility contract is a prose sentence enforced by a substring assertion, and no test asserts a nonzero semantic exit code from a real binary run. An owned parser could pass every existing test while silently changing usage text, wrapping, error wording, and exit behavior. Byte-level argv, help and error goldens are therefore the precondition, not a later refinement. Two clap feature choices are load-bearing and frozen here because a naive reimplementation would change them by default: wrap_help is OFF, so help wraps at clap's fixed width rather than the terminal's, and the env feature is OFF, so no argument is populated from the environment by the parser and every environment read is hand-rolled.

alternatives_considered.option: Replace clap with an owned parser now, per the plan's OWN (SAFE) disposition.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The plan's own re-scope calls it XL: roughly 33.8k lines across six sources with hundreds of attribute sites, and an owned parser must cover OsString and invalid UTF-8, the bare double-dash terminator, short clusters, negative values, global and flattened args, counts, custom parsers, defaults, value delimiters and enums, help text and exit codes. None of that has a behavioral baseline today, so parity is currently unmeasurable.

alternatives_considered.option: Treat the existing source-hash pins as the drift boundary and proceed.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The registry says so itself: a hash match is inventory evidence, not behavioral parity. Hashes detect that a file changed; they cannot tell whether usage text, option spelling, wrapping, error wording or an exit path changed meaning. They also cannot survive the replacement they are meant to gate, since an owned parser rewrites those files entirely.

alternatives_considered.option: Unify all four binaries on the shared ExitCode registry as part of the parser work.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Desirable but it is a user-visible behavior change, not a refactor. Only the asupersync binary consumes the registry today; atp returns std ExitCode SUCCESS or FAILURE, atpd returns a Result so a failure exits 1 through Rust's default Termination, and offline_tuner calls process::exit(1) directly. Scripts and CI already depend on those observed codes. Unification must be its own reviewed change with its own evidence, and this ADR freezes the current asymmetry so the change cannot happen silently.

alternatives_considered.option: Adopt the command vocabulary in src/cli/atp_command_tree.rs as part of the frozen CLI surface.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It is unreachable. No binary imports it: its only consumers are atp_config.rs, atp_workflows.rs and the module re-export. Its twenty-two commands, including config, ci, dataset, fuzz, release and archive, cannot be typed by any user today. Freezing them would invent a user-facing contract that does not exist, and would let a future refactor silently promote them.

alternatives_considered.option: Drop the tracing-integration edge from the cli feature to reduce the marginal graph.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The plan flags this as part of this ADR, and the bead requires defining tracing subscriber initialization so that removing env_logger or clap does not silence useful diagnostics. Dropping the edge without first specifying the replacement initialization would remove operator diagnostics. Deferred to the implementation campaign with that requirement attached.

The registry contract already parses this file and asserts equality with the artifact, which makes it the strongest existing CLI contract.

preserved_config_semantics.name: binary_manifest_stanzas
preserved_config_semantics.contract: The four installed binaries are asupersync requiring cli, atp requiring atp-cli, atpd requiring atpd-daemon, and offline_tuner requiring cli and simd-intrinsics. Binary names, paths and required-features are user-visible and may not change silently.

preserved_config_semantics.contract: NO_COLOR takes precedence over CLICOLOR_FORCE, and a non-terminal stdout disables color. The -c/--color flag accepts auto and automatic, always and on and yes and true, never and off and no and false.

preserved_config_semantics.contract: CI being set selects JSON, then a non-terminal stdout selects JSON, then ASUPERSYNC_OUTPUT_FORMAT is consulted, otherwise Human. This ordering is the machine-consumer contract.

preserved_config_semantics.contract: The shared flags are format, color, verbose as a repeatable count, quiet, debug and config, with the documented short forms. COMMON_ARGS_HELP is the only frozen help text and its content is part of the contract.

preserved_config_semantics.name: exit_code_semantics
preserved_config_semantics.contract: Success is zero, user error one, runtime error two, internal error three, cancelled four, partial success five, and the testing codes are ten through thirteen. Values outside zero through one hundred twenty-five collapse to internal error. Codes may be added; existing values may not be reassigned.

preserved_config_semantics.name: current_exit_adoption_asymmetry
preserved_config_semantics.contract: Only asupersync uses the shared registry today. atp yields zero or one through std ExitCode, atpd yields one on error through the default Termination, and offline_tuner calls process::exit with one. This asymmetry is frozen as observed behavior so that unifying it becomes a deliberate reviewed change rather than silent drift.

preserved_config_semantics.name: environment_reads
preserved_config_semantics.surface: hand-rolled environment access across the CLI
preserved_config_semantics.contract: The CLI reads at least CI, ASUPERSYNC_OUTPUT_FORMAT, NO_COLOR, CLICOLOR_FORCE, SHELL, HOME, USERPROFILE, HOMEDRIVE, HOMEPATH, APPDATA, XDG_CONFIG_HOME, PROGRAMDATA, HOSTNAME, COMPUTERNAME, SSL_CERT_FILE, SSL_CERT_DIR, ATP_RQ_AUTH_KEY_HEX, ASUPERSYNC_ATP_WORKFLOW_ROOT and RUST_LOG. Path-bearing variables are sanitized before use.

preserved_config_semantics.name: stream_routing
preserved_config_semantics.contract: Data goes to stdout and progress to stderr, and each consults its own stream's terminal state. Redirecting one must not silence or corrupt the other.

preserved_config_semantics.name: hidden_command_visibility
preserved_config_semantics.contract: The two double-underscore-prefixed commands are hidden from help but remain typable. Their hidden status and their exact spelling are both part of the contract.

preserved_config_semantics.name: alias_preservation
preserved_config_semantics.contract: serve remains accepted as a documented alias for recv.

known_gaps.summary: Four of the eight source_owners entries across the CAP-CLI rows do not own the code they are credited with. src/cli/mod.rs contains zero clap references and is a pure re-export facade. src/cli/signal.rs contains zero clap references and is not used by atpd at all, which implements its own signal listener against signal_hook. Cargo.toml is the manifest rather than source. src/cli/atp_command_tree.rs is clap-dense but unreachable from any binary.
known_gaps.consequence: Every CAP-CLI row names at least one wrong file, so a baseline built from these rows would inventory a facade, an unused module, a manifest and an unreachable tree while missing src/cli/args.rs and src/cli/output.rs, which hold the only frozen help text and the entire color and format contract.

known_gaps.summary: The registry's hash-pinned snapshot list and its source_owners lists disagree. src/cli/args.rs is hash-pinned but is not a source owner of any capability row, while src/cli/mod.rs and src/cli/signal.rs are source owners but are not hash-pinned.
known_gaps.consequence: Neither list alone is a complete inventory, and a reader cannot tell which is authoritative.

known_gaps.summary: The shared exit-code registry is consumed by only one of the four binaries. atp returns std ExitCode SUCCESS or FAILURE, atpd returns a Result so failures exit one through the default Termination, and offline_tuner calls process::exit with one directly.
known_gaps.consequence: The semantic exit-code set is aspirational for three of four binaries. Any claim that the CLI has a unified exit contract is currently false, and scripts depending on the observed codes would break if unification happened silently.

known_gaps.summary: The registry records the two hidden atp commands without their double-underscore prefix, so the recorded names are not the names a user types.
known_gaps.consequence: An implementer working from the registry would build the wrong command spellings.

known_gaps.summary: The registry pins exactly ten environment variables, but the CLI demonstrably reads at least nine more, including CI, SHELL, XDG_CONFIG_HOME, APPDATA, USERPROFILE, HOMEDRIVE, HOMEPATH, ASUPERSYNC_ATP_WORKFLOW_ROOT and RUST_LOG. The count assertion passes only because the test checks names against the seven hash-pinned sources, which exclude output.rs, first_run.rs and completion.rs where several of those reads live.
known_gaps.consequence: The environment contract is materially incomplete, and the test that appears to guard it cannot detect the omissions.

known_gaps.summary: No help golden exists. No test captures --help, -h or --version output for any of the four binaries. The help, OsString and accessibility contract is a prose sentence in the artifact, enforced only by asserting that the sentence contains the substring shell/OsString.
known_gaps.consequence: This is the central blocker for a parser replacement. Usage text, option spelling, wrapping, ordering and error wording are precisely what an owned parser would change, and nothing would detect it.

known_gaps.summary: There is no explicit handling or test for non-UTF-8 argv. Invalid UTF-8 is handled only implicitly by clap's PathBuf value parsers and one default_value_os_t. There is no allow_invalid_utf8 setting, no explicit OsString value parser and no test.
known_gaps.consequence: The OsString half of the claimed contract has no behavioral evidence, on any platform.

known_gaps.summary: No test asserts a nonzero semantic exit code from a real binary invocation. Existing real-binary tests assert success only.
known_gaps.consequence: The failure half of the exit contract is unproven end to end, which is the half operators and CI actually depend on.

known_gaps.summary: The CAP-CLI-OFFLINE-TUNER row claims the benchmark-adapters feature, but the binary's required-features are only cli and simd-intrinsics. Separately the CAP-CLI-ATP row claims tls-native-roots, while atp-cli pulls tls and rustls-native-certs directly rather than that feature. The registry documentation also states fourteen binaries while the artifact and its test say fifteen.
known_gaps.consequence: Feature and platform matrices built from these rows would test the wrong cells.

known_gaps.summary: The accessibility constraints that exist in code belong to the doctor TUI visual-language contract, not to CLI help output. They govern rendered screens, including alert-role distinguishability and avoiding motion-only state signals.
known_gaps.consequence: They must not be cited as evidence for the CLI accessibility contract, which currently has no executable coverage beyond the color and format resolution functions.

cancellation_invariants: Interrupt and broken-pipe produce a clean exit rather than a panic or a partial write mistaken for success.
Partial outputs are identified as partial, which is what the partial-success code exists for.
Signals cause a bounded structured drain with an explicit second-signal policy, and no child work survives the parent.
Progress reporting on stderr stops cleanly when stdout is closed.
