adrs.title: Preserve Brotli RFC 7932 capability; KEEP incumbent until a full owned parity campaign passes
adrs.decision_summary: The focused pure-Rust brotli dependency stays, alongside flate2. The owner directive was already resolved in favour of KEEP before this ADR, and nothing in the source read argues against it. What the read adds is the precise scope a future parity campaign would have to match, and two corrections. First, the real codec lives entirely in src/http/compress.rs, which holds every brotli and flate2 call, the encoding enum, the negotiation algorithm, and the bomb-bound enforcement; the registry names src/web/compress.rs instead, whose only brotli references are inside its test module. Second, src/net/atp/compress/ looks like a second Brotli implementation with adapters and an engine, but it is orphaned: no module declares it, nothing references it, and one of its functions would not even compile on a default build because it imports flate2 without a feature gate. Anyone estimating the replacement from a naive grep would double-count a directory that has never compiled.

alternatives_considered.option: Remove Brotli and support only gzip and deflate.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Brotli is a live public capability in three places: HTTP Accept-Encoding negotiation, the public BrotliCompressor and BrotliDecompressor types, and the ATP manifest compression algorithm. It is also the default first preference in both compression middlewares. Removal reduces interoperability with every browser that advertises br, and the capability registry's no-claim boundary states outright that DEFLATE parity does not cover Brotli.

alternatives_considered.option: Write an owned RFC 7932 encoder and decoder now.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Only as a separate security-sensitive codec epic. The scope is an encoder and decoder, quality and window settings, streaming flush and finalization, output limits, interoperability with multiple producers and consumers, both HTTP and ATP behavior, a malformed and bomb corpus, and performance and maintenance cost. Compression codecs are a classic source of memory-safety and resource-exhaustion bugs, which is why this cannot ride along with unrelated dependency work.

alternatives_considered.option: Treat Brotli as cleanup that rides along with the DEFLATE campaign.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: This is the specific failure mode the bead exists to prevent. The two codecs share a module and a feature flag but not a risk profile or an evidence corpus. Bundling them would let a DEFLATE parity result be read as authorising a Brotli removal.

alternatives_considered.option: Reuse the CompressionEngine and BrotliAdapter under src/net/atp/compress/ as the basis for an owned implementation.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: That code is orphaned and has never compiled. No module declares it, nothing outside the directory references its types, and its gzip path imports flate2 with no feature gate, which would be a hard error on a default build. It is not a partial implementation and must not be counted as one.

alternatives_considered.option: Make the compression feature default-on to simplify the matrix.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Out of scope and a graph-size change in the wrong direction. The feature is correctly opt-in, and the identity path plus negotiation work without it.

preserved_public_symbols.note: The ungated half: the encoding vocabulary, the negotiation algorithm, the codec traits and the factory all exist without the compression feature. The factory returns None for the three real codings when the feature is off, so a build without it still negotiates and still serves identity.
The real codecs and the only place brotli and flate2 are called. This file is absent from the capability registry's source_owners, which is CMP-GAP-01.

The policy-bearing middleware. It owns the BREACH sensitivity guard and the only path that returns 406 when nothing acceptable can be produced. Its production code contains no brotli or flate2 reference; it delegates to http::compress.

A second, parallel compression middleware whose type name collides with the one in web::compress. It has no BREACH guard and no 406 path; it falls back to an uncompressed body. Both are public and both are frozen, because a consumer may be using either.
The ATP manifest capability the plan cites as a reason to keep brotli. Its Brotli branch is feature-gated with an explicit None stub when compression is off.
gRPC frame compression, gzip only. Frozen because it shares the compression feature flag, so a feature change reaches it too.

preserved_feature_flags.no_tokio_guarantee: Both codecs are pure Rust with no tokio edge.

preserved_feature_flags.no_tokio_guarantee: Pure Rust, no tokio edge. No brotli type appears in any public signature.

preserved_surfaces.note: Entirely owned and dependency-free, so it survives any codec replacement. Implements the RFC 9110 identity rules, accepts the x-gzip alias, and breaks quality ties by server preference order.

preserved_surfaces.transport: HTTP response bodies and ATP manifests
preserved_surfaces.note: The capability this ADR exists to protect. Streaming chunk-at-a-time with explicit finish, poisoning on error, and quality and window exposed as plain integers rather than crate types.

preserved_surfaces.transport: HTTP response bodies, gRPC frames, ATP storage
preserved_surfaces.note: Separate campaign from Brotli. Note the level constructors take flate2::Compression, so a flate2 replacement is a public API change while a brotli replacement is not.

Owned and codec-independent. The limiting writer refuses a write that would exceed the budget before extending the buffer, so a decompression bomb never allocates. Every codec wraps it, in both directions.

Skips compression for responses correlated with secrets, keyed on request cookie or authorization or CSRF headers, a set-cookie response header, or a private or no-store or no-cache cache-control. Present in only one of the two middlewares.

src/net/atp/compress/ contains an engine, an algorithm registry and a Brotli adapter, but no module declares the directory and nothing references its types, so it never compiles. Its gzip function imports flate2 without a feature gate, which confirms it is not built. Recorded so it is neither counted as an implementation nor as replacement scope.
There is no zstd dependency and no zstd encoding. The token is deliberately used in tests as the canonical unknown coding. Recorded so the four supported codings are not mistaken for an open set.

preserved_wire_contract.protocol: HTTP content coding, plus ATP manifest compression
preserved_wire_contract.encoding: identity, gzip including the x-gzip alias, deflate as zlib-wrapped RFC 1951, and Brotli RFC 7932
preserved_wire_contract.signal_paths_note: Successful compression removes content-length, sets content-encoding, and merges rather than replaces the Vary header. Responses with 204 or 304, or an already-set content-encoding, are skipped, as is output that is not smaller than the input.
preserved_wire_contract.http_status_semantics: When a header is present and nothing acceptable can be produced, the policy-bearing middleware returns 406 with an explicit body. The parallel middleware instead returns the body uncompressed. Both behaviors are frozen.
preserved_wire_contract.collector_interop: Browsers and intermediaries advertising br must continue to receive Brotli.
preserved_wire_contract.negotiation_rules: Quality values accept both lower and upper case q, out-of-range or non-finite values drop the entry, a missing q defaults to one, identity defaults to one unless explicitly scored or suppressed by a zero wildcard, and a non-zero wildcard does not lower the identity default. Ties break by server preference order.

preserved_config_semantics.name: supported_encoding_order
preserved_config_semantics.contract: Both default to Brotli, then gzip, then deflate, then identity. Because ties break by server preference, this ordering is the observable default behavior and may not be reordered silently.

preserved_config_semantics.name: minimum_body_size
preserved_config_semantics.contract: Defaults to 256 bytes; smaller bodies are not compressed.

preserved_config_semantics.name: output_size_limit
preserved_config_semantics.contract: Defaults to 16 MiB. None means unlimited and must remain expressible. The limit applies to both compression and decompression.

preserved_config_semantics.name: brotli_parameters
preserved_config_semantics.contract: Quality and window are plain integers with documented defaults of quality 5 and window 22. Exposing them as integers rather than crate types is what keeps brotli out of the public API.

preserved_config_semantics.name: codec_poisoning
preserved_config_semantics.contract: After any error a decompressor is poisoned: its buffer is cleared and every later call returns the same explicit error. A poisoned codec must never resume and appear to succeed.

preserved_config_semantics.name: error_type
preserved_config_semantics.contract: All failures are std::io::Error. Limit violations use InvalidData with a distinct message for compressed versus decompressed overflow. No brotli type appears in any public signature.

preserved_config_semantics.name: sensitivity_default
preserved_config_semantics.contract: Sensitive responses are not compressed by default; enabling it is an explicit opt-in.

preserved_config_semantics.name: feature_off_behavior
preserved_config_semantics.contract: Without the compression feature the factory returns None for the three real codings while negotiation and identity keep working. Building without the feature must never fail to serve.

known_gaps.summary: The capability registry names src/web/compress.rs and Cargo.toml as source owners. The real codec file, src/http/compress.rs, holds every brotli and flate2 call plus the encoding enum, the negotiation algorithm, the codec traits and the bomb bounds, and is absent. The named file's only brotli references are inside its test module, so its production code contains no dependency-level compression code at all.
known_gaps.consequence: A baseline or inventory built from that row would read a middleware that merely delegates, and would miss the entire implementation. src/web/middleware.rs, src/atp/manifest.rs and src/grpc/codec.rs are also unnamed.

known_gaps.summary: src/net/atp/compress/ contains a compression engine, an algorithm registry and a Brotli adapter, but the directory is declared by no module and referenced by nothing. Its gzip function imports flate2 with no feature gate, which would be a hard compile error on a default build if it were live.
known_gaps.consequence: It looks like a second Brotli implementation. Anyone scoping a replacement from a grep would double-count roughly four files of code that has never compiled.

known_gaps.summary: The registry's baseline command names a web_compression scenario, but no compression scenario is registered in the e2e runner and the fixture is still marked planned.
known_gaps.consequence: The named baseline command does not currently exercise compression at all, so citing it as evidence would be citing a command that does nothing for this capability.

known_gaps.summary: Two public types named CompressionMiddleware exist, one in web::compress and one in web::middleware, with different behavior. Only the former has the BREACH sensitivity guard and the 406 path; the latter silently returns an uncompressed body.
known_gaps.consequence: A consumer can pick the weaker one by accident, and a security property present in one is absent in the other. Both are frozen here because both are public, but the divergence is a real defect.

known_gaps.summary: flate2::Compression appears in public signatures on the gzip and deflate level constructors, whereas brotli exposes no crate type anywhere.
known_gaps.consequence: The two codecs have asymmetric replacement cost. Replacing flate2 is a breaking public API change; replacing brotli is not. Any combined estimate that treats them alike is wrong.

known_gaps.summary: There is no Brotli-specific fuzz target. Brotli is fuzzed only inside the shared HTTP decompression target.
known_gaps.consequence: For a security-sensitive codec whose replacement would be a new attack surface, dedicated malformed and bomb corpora are a precondition rather than a refinement.

known_gaps.summary: The capability registry records evidence as planned while the capability baseline artifact records the same capability as executable and complete.
known_gaps.consequence: Two governance artifacts disagree about whether a baseline exists. The same disagreement affects CAP-FUTURES-STREAMS, so it is a systemic artifact-consistency problem rather than a one-off.

security_invariants: Compression bombs are bounded by construction: the limiting writer refuses an oversized write before extending its buffer, in both directions.
The sensitive-body policy is preserved, so responses correlated with secrets are not compressed by default.
A codec poisoned by an earlier error never resumes and never presents partial output as complete.
Brotli remains supported, so no peer advertising br is silently downgraded.
No unsafe algorithmic shortcut is introduced in any codec path.
cancellation_invariants: A cancelled body releases codec state rather than leaking an encoder.
A truncated stream is never presented as a complete body; finish is explicit and separate from chunked writes.
Streaming backpressure is preserved because codecs operate chunk-at-a-time rather than buffering whole bodies.

platform_cells.note: Both codecs are pure Rust with no platform-specific paths and no C dependency.

asupersync::http::compress codec types for direct use
the two public compression middlewares

user_journeys.description: A browser sends Accept-Encoding including br and receives a Brotli-encoded response with the correct Content-Encoding and a merged Vary header.
A client expresses quality preferences and the server honours them, falling back to server preference order only on a tie.
A client that accepts nothing compressible still receives a correct identity response, and a client that explicitly rejects identity receives 406 from the policy-bearing middleware.
A malicious peer sends a compression bomb and the decompressor refuses before allocating, returning a distinct size-limit error and poisoning the codec.
A response correlated with a session cookie or an authorization header is not compressed by default, mitigating BREACH-style oracles.
An ATP manifest records Brotli as its compression algorithm and the compressed length is computed for the policy.
A consumer builds without the compression feature, still negotiates encodings, and still serves identity responses without failure.

adrs.title: Preserve complete NKey credential, prefix, signing, verification and downstream API capability
adrs.decision_summary: nkeys stays. The source read reframes the replacement in three ways that all point the same direction. First, scope: the plan's design section sizes the work at roughly two hundred lines of base32, CRC-16 and prefix codec and frames it as NATS-only, but nkeys is load-bearing in four independent subsystems, not one, and the registry demands every prefix form, Curve keys, JWT signer policy and secret zeroization. Those are not the same order of magnitude. Second, direction of trade: ed25519-dalek is not a direct dependency today, it arrives only through nkeys, so the swap adds a direct cryptographic dependency plus hand-written credential-encoding code in exchange for removing one crate. For a security capability that is a materially different proposition than a net reduction. Third, readiness: the differential oracle that would prove parity does not exist, its harness directory is absent, nkeys is not a dev-dependency so it cannot yet serve as the reference, and the declared independent security review has not happened.

alternatives_considered.option: Implement the owned codec now, per the plan's Phase-4 design.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The design is scoped to a base32, CRC-16 and prefix codec for NATS. The real capability spans NATS messaging, ATP identity, ATP capability-token verification, agent-swarm credential admission and runtime signed-profile bundles, plus a key store with rotation and revocation. The estimate does not cover the consumers it would break.

alternatives_considered.option: Accept the replacement because it removes a crate from the graph.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It does not straightforwardly reduce trust surface. ed25519-dalek is transitive through nkeys today; the replacement makes it direct and adds hand-rolled base32 and CRC-16 in first-party code. The program's own discipline says moving unsafe or security-critical code from a mature, widely-used dependency into fresh first-party code does not inherently reduce risk without measured evidence and owner sign-off.

alternatives_considered.option: Narrow the replacement to the User prefix, since that is all production accepts.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Tempting, and it would be honest about current usage: production enforces User-only fail-closed at three sites, and Cluster and Operator appear solely as test fixtures. But the registry's scope explicitly includes every prefix form and Curve keys, and NATS interoperability means credential forms arrive from outside. Narrowing is a decision the owner must make deliberately, and this ADR records the choice rather than making it silently.

alternatives_considered.option: Keep nkeys but hide it behind an owned wrapper type to remove the public leak.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Worth doing eventually and cheap in isolation, since the leak is a single public function returning Result<nkeys::KeyPair, KeyStoreError>. But it is a breaking change for any downstream that calls sign or verify on the returned value, and the bead forbids permanent shims, so it belongs with the replacement rather than ahead of it.

alternatives_considered.option: Proceed once the codec passes NATS fixture vectors.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Those vectors do not exist. The oracle policy names a harness directory that is absent, and nkeys is a normal dependency rather than a dev-dependency, so the reference implementation is not even wired for differential testing. Parity is currently unmeasurable, exactly as with the CLI.

preserved_public_symbols.note: The largest owned surface and the location of the single public nkeys leak. active_key_pair returns Result<nkeys::KeyPair, KeyStoreError>, which is the only place an nkeys type reaches asupersync's public API. This file is absent from the capability registry's source owners.

The NATS authentication path: seed loading, nonce signing, JWT subject binding and CONNECT emission. The credential block markers are the accepted .creds text format and are part of the operator-facing contract.
Signed profile bundles sign and verify through nkeys with an explicit ed25519-nkey integrity mode. A consumer of this capability that the registry does not name.
ATP peer identity validates NKey public keys and records an nkey-ed25519 auth method. Also unnamed by the registry.
Agent admission verifies credential signatures with a pinned nkey_ed25519 scheme constant. Also unnamed by the registry.

preserved_feature_flags.name: nkeys
preserved_feature_flags.effect: Unconditional and non-optional, so NKey credential support ships in every build on every target with no feature gate. It also transitively supplies ed25519-dalek, ed25519 and data-encoding, none of which is a direct dependency.

preserved_feature_flags.name: test-internals
preserved_feature_flags.effect: Gates the doc-hidden fuzz shims that expose seed loading as a String-returning function. Those deliberately launder the type so no nkeys value escapes even through the fuzz surface.

preserved_surfaces.note: Generation-tracked keys with rotation, revocation and history. The store, its platform permission model, its domain-separated fingerprints and its seed entropy validation are all asupersync-owned; only the key type itself comes from nkeys.

The entire public nkeys surface is this one function. Everything else that touches nkeys does so behind an owned type or a private function, so the API blast radius of a replacement is small even though the internal blast radius is not.

preserved_surfaces.note: Seed loading, nonce signing, JWT subject binding with a constant-time comparison, and a required ed25519-nkey algorithm. The .creds text block markers are the accepted operator format.

preserved_surfaces.wire_encoder: nkey-ed25519 signatures over capability tokens and agent credentials
preserved_surfaces.transport: ATP protocol and swarm control plane

preserved_wire_contract.protocol: NATS authentication, ATP capability tokens, agent-swarm credentials and signed profile bundles
preserved_wire_contract.encoding: canonical NKey base32 with CRC-16/XMODEM and typed prefix bytes, over ed25519 signatures
preserved_wire_contract.signal_paths_note: NATS CONNECT carries the public key and a base64url-encoded nonce signature. Credential files use explicit BEGIN and END markers for the JWT and the seed.
preserved_wire_contract.collector_interop: Real NATS servers and clients must continue to accept and be accepted.
preserved_wire_contract.algorithm_pinning: The JWT algorithm must be ed25519-nkey, and the signed-profile and swarm schemes are pinned constants. These are fail-closed checks, not hints.
preserved_wire_contract.prefix_enforcement: Production accepts User keys only and rejects other kinds explicitly at three separate sites. That restriction is current behavior and is frozen as such.

preserved_config_semantics.name: user_only_enforcement
preserved_config_semantics.surface: key store, NATS seed loading and ATP identity validation
preserved_config_semantics.contract: All three reject a non-User key kind with an explicit error naming the kind found. Type separation between public, seed and private forms is fail-closed.

preserved_config_semantics.name: secret_redaction
preserved_config_semantics.contract: Debug output redacts the JWT and the seed, and persisted seed material never appears in diagnostics. Both are covered by dedicated tests today.

preserved_config_semantics.name: seed_entropy_validation
preserved_config_semantics.contract: Weak seed material is rejected before use, with owned thresholds. This is asupersync's own check layered on top of nkeys.

preserved_config_semantics.name: domain_separated_fingerprints
preserved_config_semantics.contract: SHA-256 fingerprints are domain-separated with an explicit constant, and a redacted rendering exists for logs. Both the domain separation and the redacted form are contract.

preserved_config_semantics.name: constant_time_comparison
preserved_config_semantics.contract: The subject comparison is constant-time. Replacing it with an ordinary equality check would be a security regression, not a refactor.

preserved_config_semantics.name: key_rotation_and_revocation
preserved_config_semantics.contract: Keys carry generations, rotation preserves history, and revocation is recorded rather than deleting the record. Export of public history must remain available.

preserved_config_semantics.name: platform_permission_model
preserved_config_semantics.contract: The store distinguishes owner-only Unix permissions, a Windows ACL requirement and a best-effort fallback. Weakening any cell is a security change.

preserved_config_semantics.name: algorithm_fail_closed
preserved_config_semantics.contract: An unexpected algorithm is rejected rather than defaulted. Signer authorization failures are distinct from signature failures and neither is oracular.

known_gaps.summary: The capability registry names src/messaging/nats.rs and Cargo.toml as source owners. Both genuinely contain nkey code, so this row is not a phantom-owner row, but it is wrong by omission: five production files with real nkey code are missing, including src/security/keys/mod.rs which hosts the only public leak, plus src/runtime/config.rs, src/atp/identity/mod.rs, src/atp/policy/verification.rs and src/agent_swarm/control_plane.rs.
known_gaps.consequence: The row makes the capability look NATS-shaped when it actually spans four independent subsystems. Any scoping built from it, including the plan's own design section, will underestimate the consumers a replacement breaks.

known_gaps.summary: The registry's dependency owners list base32 and crc16 as if they were crates. Neither exists in the manifest or the lockfile: base32 comes from data-encoding pulled in by nkeys, and CRC-16/XMODEM is implemented inside nkeys itself. The same list names ed25519-dalek as an owner although it is not a direct dependency.
known_gaps.consequence: A marginal-cost calculation or an SBOM built from that list would reference crates that are not in the graph and would misattribute the ed25519 edge.

known_gaps.summary: The differential oracle does not exist. The oracle policy names a harness directory that is absent from the tree, and nkeys is a normal dependency rather than a dev-dependency, so the reference implementation is not wired for differential testing at all.
known_gaps.consequence: Parity against the incumbent cannot currently be measured. This is the single blocking precondition for any replacement.

known_gaps.summary: There are no independent official NKey or NATS vectors in the repository. Existing tests generate their own deterministic seeds from fixed raw bytes, which proves self-consistency rather than interoperability.
known_gaps.consequence: A replacement could be self-consistent and still wrong against real NATS peers.

known_gaps.summary: The declared independent security review has not happened. The safety taxonomy records the gate with no exception record, and the capability remains at planned evidence with the incumbent kept.
known_gaps.consequence: The gate the program itself set for this capability is unmet, so no cutover discussion is in order.

known_gaps.summary: The plan's design section sizes the replacement at roughly two hundred lines covering base32, CRC-16 and prefixes, and frames it as NATS-only. The registry scopes the same capability to every prefix form, Curve and X25519 keys, JWT signer policy and secret zeroization, across four subsystems.
known_gaps.consequence: The two scopes differ by more than an order of magnitude. Planning from the smaller one would commit the project to a security-critical rewrite on a false estimate.

known_gaps.summary: Production exercises the User kind only, enforced fail-closed. Cluster and Operator appear solely as test fixtures, and Account, Server, Module, Service and Curve are not referenced anywhere in the repository.
known_gaps.consequence: Whether the replacement must preserve actual capability, which is User-only, or nominal upstream capability, which is eight kinds plus seed, private and curve encodings, is an unresolved owner decision that changes the scope enormously. Recorded rather than silently narrowed.

known_gaps.summary: The capability baseline records resource-limit evidence as blocked on an owner and cancellation-cleanup and recovery as blocked externally.
known_gaps.consequence: Bounded parse and verify behavior, and the cancellation invariant that authentication cancellation wipes transient secrets, are both unproven.

security_invariants: Sensitive comparisons are constant-time, including the JWT subject binding.
Secrets are zeroized and never cloned into ordinary APIs; debug output redacts both the JWT and the seed.
Public, seed and private forms are type-separated, and only the User kind is accepted in production, fail-closed.
Signer authorization fails closed, and an unexpected algorithm is rejected rather than defaulted.
Seed entropy is validated before use.
An independent security review is a precondition for any cutover, and it has not happened.
cancellation_invariants: Authentication cancellation releases connection state and wipes transient secrets.
A partially completed handshake never leaves a usable authenticated session.
These are stated obligations rather than proven ones; the baseline records both as blocked.

adrs.title: Preserve full futures-lite production semantics, public Stream usability, and test executor workflows
adrs.decision_summary: futures-lite stays. The classification the bead demands turns a scary number into a precise one: of roughly 796 references across 148 files under src, essentially all sit inside test modules. The production set is six sites in five files. But the shape of those six is what decides this. Exactly one is a public trait impl: AtpWriter and AtpReader implement futures_lite::Stream, which is downstream-visible and semver-relevant, and is the only impl of that foreign trait anywhere in the crate. Two are the FutureExt panic-containment boundary in the web layer. Three are the executor itself, block_on, one of them inside the body of the public non-async Router::handle and two driving signal-listener threads. The plan classifies this as a Phase-2 low-risk leaf removal over disjoint files with a util/future.rs shim; that is wrong on every count. The file set is roughly 272 including tests, not disjoint, and the proposed shim covers five helpers while missing poll_once, join_all, pending, FutureExt::catch_unwind and Stream entirely.

alternatives_considered.option: Move the helpers to an owned util/future.rs and drop futures-lite, per the plan's Phase-2 entry.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The shim list is incomplete and the framing is wrong. It names block_on, poll_fn, zip, race and yield_now, but production and tests also use poll_once, join_all and pending, and neither FutureExt::catch_unwind nor the Stream trait is a free function that a helper module can provide. The work also touches roughly 272 files rather than a disjoint few, which contradicts the phase's own parallelism premise.

alternatives_considered.option: Port AtpWriter and AtpReader to the crate's own Stream trait, removing the last public futures-lite surface.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Attractive and probably correct eventually, but it is a breaking change for any downstream already calling futures_lite::StreamExt methods on those types, and it currently has zero test coverage to protect it. It is recorded as the specific, bounded step that would remove all public leakage, and it belongs to the implementation campaign with downstream-consumer evidence attached.

alternatives_considered.option: Keep futures-lite only as a dev-dependency for tests.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Impossible as things stand. There is no dev-dependency entry today; the single unconditional entry in dependencies is what makes futures-lite visible to both src and tests. Demoting it would break the six production sites, including the public Stream impls and the executor inside Router::handle.

alternatives_considered.option: Replace the executor uses of block_on with the asupersync runtime.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The three production block_on sites are precisely where that is hardest. Router::handle is a public, documented, synchronous entry point whose whole async execution is block_on, and the two signal-listener sites run on dedicated std threads outside any runtime. Changing them alters reentrancy and nested-runtime behavior, which is exactly the contract the bead asks this ADR to define rather than to change.

alternatives_considered.option: Treat the roughly 149 non-test-file count as the migration scope.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It overstates production risk and understates total churn at the same time. Production coupling is six sites; total churn including tests is roughly 272 files. Conflating the two produces both a false sense of danger and a false sense of boundedness.

preserved_public_symbols.note: asupersync's own Stream trait, structurally identical to the ecosystem one plus a defaulted size hint, with blanket impls for pinned pointers, boxes and mutable references. Entirely free of futures-lite. This file is where the trait is defined and is absent from the registry's source owners.
The extension trait and the combinator surface, blanket-implemented for every local Stream. Roughly thirty owned combinators sit on top of it, none of which touch futures-lite.
Adapters over the local trait. Contains no futures-lite reference of any kind, which is why naming it as a futures-lite source owner is a defect rather than a rounding error.

The only place in the crate that implements the foreign futures_lite::Stream, and the whole of the public futures-lite surface. Publicly reachable with no feature gate, so the impls are semver-relevant. Notably this file does not import the crate's own Stream trait.
Panic containment is two-stage: a synchronous catch at construction, then FutureExt::catch_unwind at poll time. Only the second stage depends on futures-lite.
The error and negotiation handler's panic containment, gated by an explicit configuration flag. Uses the futures-lite stage only.

The highest-risk site. Router::handle is a public synchronous entry point whose entire async execution is futures-lite's block_on. The dependency does not appear in the signature, so this is a semantic rather than a type leak.
Two block_on calls driving signal-listener loops on dedicated std threads, outside any runtime. Replacing the executor here changes thread and reentrancy behavior.

preserved_feature_flags.name: futures-lite
preserved_feature_flags.effect: An unconditional, non-optional dependency with no feature gate and no dev-dependency entry. That single entry is what makes futures-lite visible to src, tests, benches and examples alike. It cannot be made optional or dev-only without breaking the six production sites.

preserved_feature_flags.name: default
preserved_feature_flags.effect: Recorded because the capability registry claims this capability is gated by default and test-internals. It is not gated at all: futures-lite is unconditional, so a consumer building with default features disabled still gets it and still gets the public Stream impls.

preserved_surfaces.note: A complete owned Stream implementation across roughly thirty combinators with no futures-lite dependency at the type level. This is the surface most downstream code uses, and it carries no replacement risk at all.

The entire public futures-lite surface, and the sole outlier from the crate's own trait. Any downstream can call ecosystem StreamExt methods on these types, so removing futures-lite silently deletes that capability.
FutureExt::catch_unwind is the poll-phase half of the web panic boundary. It is not a free function, so a helper-module shim cannot replace it; an owned equivalent would need its own future adapter.

Three sites, and the ones the bead's own description misses. One is inside a public synchronous API; two drive listener threads outside any runtime. These define the reentrancy and nested-runtime contract the ADR is asked to specify.

block_on accounts for the overwhelming majority of all futures-lite references and is the de facto test executor for the repository, reached directly or through per-module wrappers across roughly 272 files. There is no shared harness to swap in one place.
The util/future.rs module the plan names does not exist. Recorded so the plan entry is not read as describing something already partially built.

There is no adapter, blanket impl or conversion between the crate's Stream trait and the ecosystem one. The two coexist as disjoint, structurally identical traits. Recorded because the absence is what makes the ATP SDK outlier consequential.

preserved_wire_contract.protocol: in-process async execution; not a wire protocol
preserved_wire_contract.signal_paths_note: Router::handle is a synchronous public entry point that internally drives an async pipeline to completion, and the signal listeners drive receive loops on dedicated threads outside any runtime.
preserved_wire_contract.trait_compatibility: AtpWriter and AtpReader satisfy the ecosystem Stream trait, so downstream generic code bounded on it accepts them. That is a semver-relevant public property.

preserved_config_semantics.name: public_stream_impl
preserved_config_semantics.contract: Both implement the ecosystem Stream trait with a transfer-progress item type. Downstream generic code bounded on that trait must keep compiling, and ecosystem extension methods must keep working on these types.

preserved_config_semantics.name: owned_stream_independence
preserved_config_semantics.contract: The owned trait and its combinators must remain free of any futures-lite dependency, so the main Stream surface carries no replacement risk.

preserved_config_semantics.name: panic_containment_two_stage
preserved_config_semantics.contract: A panic during handler construction and a panic during polling are both contained, and both produce an error response rather than unwinding into the server. Only the poll-phase stage depends on futures-lite.

preserved_config_semantics.name: synchronous_public_entry
preserved_config_semantics.contract: A synchronous, non-async public entry point that drives its pipeline to completion. Its blocking behavior, and the fact that it does not require an ambient runtime, are part of the contract.

preserved_config_semantics.name: signal_listener_threads
preserved_config_semantics.contract: Listener loops run on dedicated std threads and block on receive. They must not require an ambient runtime and must not be starved by one.

preserved_config_semantics.name: test_executor_availability
preserved_config_semantics.contract: A blocking executor must remain available to every test target without extra configuration. Any replacement must offer a drop-in equivalent, because there is no central harness to change.

preserved_config_semantics.name: helper_surface_completeness
preserved_config_semantics.contract: The consumed surface is block_on, poll_fn, poll_once, zip, race, join_all, yield_now, pending, FutureExt::catch_unwind and the Stream trait. Any owned replacement must cover all of it, not the five helpers the plan names.

preserved_config_semantics.name: no_hidden_executor
preserved_config_semantics.contract: No API may start an executor implicitly. The three production block_on sites are explicit and documented, and that explicitness is the contract.

known_gaps.summary: The capability registry names src/stream/mod.rs and src/io/stream_adapters.rs as source owners. The first has exactly one futures-lite reference and it is inside a test module; the second has none at all. Every file that actually owns a production futures-lite semantic named in the row's own title, including block_on and the panic boundaries, is absent, as is src/stream/stream.rs where the owned trait is defined.
known_gaps.consequence: The two named files cover precisely the part of the capability that has no futures-lite dependency and therefore no replacement risk. A baseline built from that row would inventory the safe half and miss all six production sites.

known_gaps.summary: The public futures_lite::Stream impls for AtpWriter and AtpReader have no test. The file's test module exercises chunk construction and constructor failure paths, never invokes poll_next, and never imports an extension trait.
known_gaps.consequence: The single public futures-lite surface in the crate is the one with zero coverage, so its removal or breakage would be silent.

known_gaps.summary: The downstream consumer fixture proves the crate's own Stream trait is usable from an external crate, and does not reference futures-lite at all.
known_gaps.consequence: The existing downstream proof would not detect a futures-lite removal breaking the ATP SDK Stream impls. A second fixture bounded on the ecosystem trait is needed before any cutover.

known_gaps.summary: The registry records this capability's features as default and test-internals, but futures-lite is unconditional with no feature gate at all.
known_gaps.consequence: Any feature matrix derived from that row would test the wrong cells and could conclude the dependency is optional.

known_gaps.summary: The capability registry records evidence as planned while the capability baseline artifact records the same capability as executable and complete.
known_gaps.consequence: Two governance artifacts disagree about whether a baseline exists. The same disagreement affects CAP-HTTP-COMPRESSION, so it is systemic.

known_gaps.summary: The manifest comment on the dependency describes it as used by web handler adapter shims. That covers two of the six production sites and omits the ATP Stream impls, the router executor and the signal listeners.
known_gaps.consequence: A reader trusting the comment would underestimate both the coupling and its risk profile.

known_gaps.summary: The ATP SDK stream types are the only place in the crate that chose the ecosystem Stream trait; every other stream implementation in net, io and stream uses the crate's own trait. There is no adapter between the two.
known_gaps.consequence: The inconsistency is the entire reason futures-lite appears in the public API. Porting those two impls would remove all public leakage, at the cost of a breaking change for downstreams relying on the current impls.

adrs.title: Preserve the complete Kafka client capability behind an already rdkafka-free public facade
adrs.decision_summary: The rdkafka dependency and the kafka feature both stay. The source read turned up one strongly favorable fact and several corrections. The favorable fact is that the public API is already completely free of rdkafka types: every producer, consumer, transaction, config, security and error type is first-party, the error enum is hand-rolled with the upstream error aliased and mapped rather than re-exported, and every rdkafka value lives in a private field or a private function. rdkafka is a swappable backend behind a facade the project already owns, which is the best possible starting position and is worth stating plainly. The corrections cut the other way. The plan says to remove the feature outright once a downstream inventory finds no consumer; the registry says keep until parity and its no-claim boundary is explicit that a wire codec or a simple producer is not a Kafka client. The registry governs. Removal would also delete a capability that is currently gated behind a downstream census nobody has run. Two capability gaps are worth freezing now because they bound what parity even means: there is no way to send consumer offsets inside a transaction, so read-process-write exactly-once is not covered, and there is no admin surface at all. Finally, the compression story is softer than the enum suggests: the codecs are declared in first-party code but their availability depends on what the bundled C library's configure step autodetects on the build host, not on any Cargo feature.

alternatives_considered.option: Remove the kafka feature after a downstream inventory confirms no consumer, per the plan.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The inventory has not been run, and the registry's terminal posture is keep-until-parity with a no-claim boundary stating librdkafka stays until the complete campaign and a real broker matrix pass. Removing a working, security-hardened client because a census came back empty trades a real capability for a package count.

alternatives_considered.option: Write a native Kafka client now to evict the bundled C.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The plan itself descopes this to an independent protocol campaign, and rightly. The surface to match includes API-version negotiation, flexible and tagged fields, coordinator protocols, idempotence epochs and sequences, transactions, isolation levels, offset management, compression codecs, TLS and SASL, metadata refresh and retry semantics. That is a program, not a dependency swap.

alternatives_considered.option: Treat the first-party RecordBatch v2 codec in the conformance crate as partial progress toward a native client.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It is a genuine, rdkafka-free codec and useful as conformance evidence, but a record-batch encoder is not a client. Counting it as progress is exactly the confusion the registry's no-claim boundary was written to prevent.

alternatives_considered.option: Feature-gate the module declarations so the types vanish without the feature.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The current arrangement is deliberate and better: the types exist on every build and the no-feature lane fails closed with a dedicated feature-disabled error and a diagnostic helper. Callers get a typed, explanatory failure instead of a missing module.

alternatives_considered.option: Add the missing transactional-offset and admin surfaces as part of this ADR.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: This is a decision-only ADR and adding public API is out of scope. Both are recorded as frozen gaps so a future replacement cannot quietly define parity as matching today's incomplete surface.

preserved_public_symbols.note: The module declaration is NOT feature-gated, so every one of these types exists on a default build; only broker behavior is gated. Without the feature the client fails closed with a dedicated feature-disabled error plus a diagnostic helper. KafkaClient, BrokerBackend and KafkaConsumerTrait have both a real and a deterministic implementation selected by cfg. No rdkafka type appears in any of these signatures.

The consumer half, and the second rdkafka source owner the registry omits. RebalanceResult is public and is the return type of the public rebalance method, but is reachable only through this module path because the messaging facade does not re-export it. Rebalancing is a caller-driven assignment API rather than an upstream rebalance callback, which is a deliberate determinism choice.

The facade re-export set. Two consumer types are re-exported under renamed identifiers, and the security, client, backend-trait and rebalance-result types are deliberately not re-exported. Both the renames and the omissions are part of the frozen surface.

preserved_feature_flags.name: kafka
preserved_feature_flags.effect: Switches the client from the fail-closed deterministic lane to the real broker backend. It does not gate the module or the types, only the behavior.
preserved_feature_flags.no_tokio_guarantee: rdkafka is taken with default features off, so its tokio default is not enabled and the lockfile shows no tokio edge. Any change to that flag must re-verify the no-tokio production guarantee.

preserved_feature_flags.name: rdkafka
preserved_feature_flags.cargo_definition: rdkafka = { version = "0.39", default-features = false, optional = true }
preserved_feature_flags.effect: The client backend. Default features are off and none are added back, which is what keeps tokio and the compression shim crates out of the graph.
preserved_feature_flags.no_tokio_guarantee: Turning any default feature back on risks reintroducing a tokio edge and must be re-verified against the production graph lane.

preserved_surfaces.note: Async send with and without headers, delivery metadata, acks, batching, linger, retries and message-size limits. Idempotence defaults to on.

A full lifecycle state machine with idle, active, finalizing and needs-abort-recovery phases, a drop guard, and idempotence forced on for transactional producers. Producer-side only: consumer offsets cannot join a transaction.

Subscription, caller-driven rebalance with generation and revocation tracking, manual commits, seek, and isolation level. Auto-commit is forced off in the real backend with a written rationale; that default is part of the contract.

TLS with CA, certificate, key and key password, plus SCRAM over SSL. SASL over plaintext is deliberately not exposed, non-loopback plaintext is refused with an IPv4-mapped-IPv6 bypass defense, secrets zeroize on drop and redact in debug output, and the insecure opt-out is test-only. This is a hardened posture and every part of it is frozen.

Owned and rdkafka-free. Without the feature, production paths fail closed with a typed feature-disabled error and an actionable diagnostic, while a cfg-gated deterministic in-process broker covers the state machines for tests only. Deleting the feature would delete this too.
A genuine first-party RecordBatch v2 encoder and decoder with no rdkafka dependency. Useful conformance evidence, but a codec is not a client and it may not be counted as replacement progress.

No way to send consumer offsets to a transaction, so read-process-write exactly-once is not covered. Recorded so parity is measured against the complete capability rather than against today's surface.
No topic, partition, ACL, config or group administration surface exists anywhere in the client.

preserved_wire_contract.protocol: Apache Kafka binary protocol, spoken by the bundled librdkafka
preserved_wire_contract.signal_paths_note: Produce, fetch, and the group-coordinator protocols all traverse the same backend.
preserved_wire_contract.retry_jitter: Retries and request timeout are configurable on the producer and consumer.
preserved_wire_contract.collector_interop: Interoperates with any broker the bundled library supports, across its full accepted API-version range.
preserved_wire_contract.native_build: The backend links a bundled librdkafka built through its own configure and make, not cmake. This is lockfile-verified: no cmake crate resolves and the only build-time helper that resolves is a pkg-config discovery shim. The plan records this as a corrected earlier error and it must stay lockfile-verified.
preserved_wire_contract.compression_availability: The codec enum is first-party, but which codecs the bundled library can actually use is decided by what its configure step autodetects on the build host, since default features are off and no compression shim crates resolve. Codec availability is therefore a host property, not a declared Cargo feature.

preserved_config_semantics.name: types_exist_without_the_feature
preserved_config_semantics.contract: Module declarations are not feature-gated, so the public types compile on every build and the feature switches behavior only. Callers without the feature get a typed failure, not a missing module.

preserved_config_semantics.name: fail_closed_without_the_feature
preserved_config_semantics.contract: Production paths without the feature return the dedicated feature-disabled error, and the deterministic in-process broker is reachable only under test configurations. Production must never silently reach a fake broker.

preserved_config_semantics.name: idempotence_on_by_default
preserved_config_semantics.contract: Idempotent production defaults to enabled, and is forced on for transactional producers regardless of what the caller set.

preserved_config_semantics.name: manual_commit_default
preserved_config_semantics.contract: Auto-commit is forced off with a written rationale. Consumers commit explicitly, which is what makes at-least-once and read-committed reasoning tractable.

preserved_config_semantics.name: no_sasl_over_plaintext
preserved_config_semantics.contract: Only SCRAM over SSL is exposed. SASL over plaintext is deliberately absent and must not be added as a convenience.

preserved_config_semantics.name: plaintext_refused_off_loopback
preserved_config_semantics.contract: A plaintext bootstrap server that is not loopback is refused, including via IPv4-mapped-IPv6 forms. The opt-out is a test-only builder method and must stay that way.

preserved_config_semantics.name: credential_hygiene
preserved_config_semantics.contract: SASL passwords zeroize on drop, and both SASL passwords and TLS key passwords are redacted in debug output.

preserved_config_semantics.name: caller_driven_rebalance
preserved_config_semantics.contract: Assignment is caller-driven and returns generation, assigned and revoked sets, rather than firing an upstream rebalance callback. This is a determinism choice and callers depend on the returned shape.

adrs.title: Keep the SQLite feature; any FrankenSQLite path must be cycle-safe, official, and equally discoverable
adrs.decision_summary: The sqlite feature stays, with rusqlite and its bundled C. The governing fact is structural rather than a matter of taste: FrankenSQLite depends on asupersync, so asupersync cannot depend back without a Cargo cycle. That means the replacement engine cannot be an in-workspace oracle, cannot be a dev-dependency, and cannot be reached by the root feature. Parity must be measured in the downstream repository or in a neutral consumer depending on both. Two corrections matter. First, the bead's own wording says FrankenSQLite depends optionally on asupersync; the downstream manifest has no optional marker and the plan states the dependency is unconditional. The bead text is wrong and this ADR does not carry it forward. Second, the plan's section 9.1 says the feature is deprecated or removed and the integration inverted, while the registry and the bead both make KEEP the default terminal result unless an owner approves an equally discoverable public move. The registry governs. On the code itself the news is good: the async wrapper is a genuinely well-built seam, with a single blocking-pool funnel, a real interrupt on cancel, and a masked drain that refuses to report cancelled until the blocking job acknowledges. Exactly one rusqlite type reaches the public API, and it does so through a foreign-trait impl rather than a signature, which is easy to miss and hard to remove.

alternatives_considered.option: Deprecate or remove the sqlite feature and invert the integration into FrankenSQLite, per plan section 9.1.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The bead is explicit that removing the feature after merely proving downstream parity would worsen discoverability and force users to reconstruct the integration themselves. Cargo cannot make the root feature depend on the downstream adapter without a cycle, so the default terminal result is KEEP unless an owner approves an equally discoverable public move after user-journey trials.

alternatives_considered.option: Add FrankenSQLite as a dev-dependency so parity can be measured in-workspace.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Forbidden outright. The registry's no-claim boundary states it may not be added back as an asupersync dependency or used as an in-workspace oracle, and the oracle policy names the cycle rule explicitly. This is not a preference; it is a package-graph impossibility.

alternatives_considered.option: Swap the engine and keep the current public types unchanged.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: One rusqlite type is already public through a foreign-trait impl on a public value type. That impl cannot survive an engine swap without an equivalent trait, so the swap is semver-breaking whether or not any signature mentions the engine.

alternatives_considered.option: Count the existing SQLite end-to-end suite as the parity oracle.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It exercises one engine. Parity means the same suite running on both engines during an overlap period, which by the cycle rule cannot happen in this workspace.

alternatives_considered.option: Treat the smaller marginal package count as sufficient justification.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The plan itself calls this capability relocation rather than zero dependency cost, and requires a combined consumer budget measured with the program's own ledger. A count taken on one side of the relocation is not a budget.

preserved_feature_flags.name: rusqlite
preserved_feature_flags.effect: The engine. The bundled feature compiles the C amalgamation through a native build script; the hooks feature is what makes the progress handler available, and the budget-derived statement timeout is built on it. Neither may be dropped casually.

preserved_feature_flags.name: sqlparser
preserved_feature_flags.effect: Backs the checked SQL surface that separates the validated methods from the unchecked ones. It also drags in a recursion helper that carries C and assembly stack-probing code, so it is a second native edge and not merely a parser.

preserved_surfaces.note: Open on disk or in memory, execute, batch, query, single-row query and row streaming, all taking the capability context. Parameters cross the boundary as the owned value type, never as an engine type.

Deferred, immediate and exclusive begins, with three-deep savepoint nesting covered by tests. The drop path discharges the obligation token and poisons for rollback, and a generation counter prevents a stale finish job from touching a newer transaction.

The best-engineered part of this surface and entirely owned. On cancel the pool task is marked, a real interrupt is issued, and the operation then enters a bounded masked drain: it does not report cancelled until the blocking job acknowledges, so the connection lock is released and no statement keeps running unobserved. The row stream carries its own interrupt handle so dropping it aborts a long step rather than waiting for the next row boundary. Three drain outcomes are distinguished and traced.

The effective limit is the minimum of the remaining context budget and any per-connection override, enforced through the engine's progress handler. Arming failure is fatal to the operation by design, because running unbounded after a bound was requested would void the contract. A documented caveat stands: the handler runs only while the virtual machine executes, so time blocked on a locked database can overshoot by up to the busy timeout.

The default methods validate the SQL surface through the parser and reject unsafe constructs with dedicated error variants; the unchecked variants are the explicit opt-out. The pairing is the security contract and both halves are frozen.

The single public leak, and it is easy to miss: a public implementation of the engine's own parameter-binding trait on the owned value type. No signature names the engine, yet the API is semver-coupled to it. An engine swap cannot preserve this without an equivalent trait.

Forbidden by the cycle rule, not merely absent. The downstream project depends on asupersync unconditionally, so it may not be added back as a dependency or used as an in-workspace oracle. The corresponding fixture row is marked unsupported for the same reason.

The companion workspace or published integration crate that would make a downstream engine equally discoverable does not exist. Until it does, the feature is the only one-stop supported path and removing it would strand users.

preserved_config_semantics.name: checked_by_default_unchecked_by_choice
preserved_config_semantics.contract: Default methods validate the SQL surface and reject unsafe constructs with dedicated error variants; the unchecked variants are an explicit opt-out. Neither half may be dropped, and the default must not become unchecked.

preserved_config_semantics.name: effective_timeout_is_a_minimum
preserved_config_semantics.contract: The enforced limit is the minimum of the remaining context budget and any per-connection override. A per-connection override cannot extend a shorter budget.

preserved_config_semantics.name: timeout_arming_failure_is_fatal
preserved_config_semantics.contract: If the progress handler cannot be armed, the operation fails rather than running unbounded. Silently proceeding without the requested bound would void the contract.

preserved_config_semantics.name: cancel_drains_before_reporting
preserved_config_semantics.contract: On cancellation the operation issues a real interrupt and then waits, under a bounded masked drain, for the blocking job to acknowledge before reporting cancelled. The three drain outcomes — job completed, job never started, and drain budget exhausted — are distinguished and traced.

preserved_config_semantics.name: stream_owns_its_interrupt
preserved_config_semantics.contract: The row stream carries its own interrupt handle so dropping or cancelling it aborts an in-flight step rather than waiting for the next row boundary.

preserved_config_semantics.name: transaction_drop_rolls_back
preserved_config_semantics.contract: Dropping an unfinished transaction discharges the obligation token and poisons for rollback, and the rollback is generation-guarded so a stale finish job cannot affect a newer transaction.

preserved_config_semantics.name: error_predicates_are_the_retry_contract
preserved_config_semantics.contract: The busy, locked, constraint, unique, connection, transient and retryable predicates and the error-code accessor are how callers classify failures. Their classifications are frozen.

preserved_config_semantics.name: engine_errors_do_not_cross_the_boundary
preserved_config_semantics.contract: Engine errors are stringified into the owned taxonomy rather than wrapped. No engine error type is reachable from the public API.

preserved_config_semantics.name: hooks_feature_is_load_bearing
preserved_config_semantics.contract: The timeout mechanism depends on the engine's hooks feature. Dropping it to trim the graph would silently remove statement timeouts.

adrs.title: Owned UTC timestamp/calendar surface for full chrono/time capability, serialization, and UX
adrs.decision_summary: An owned UTC timestamp type may be built additively, but chrono and the time crate stay until it demonstrably parses the existing persisted corpus. The bead was right that the one-helper estimate is invalid, and the source read shows why in a specific way. The time crate genuinely has exactly one call site, private and non-leaking, so the plan is correct about it. chrono is a different matter: ten public serde-derived fields typed as a chrono UTC datetime across three public modules, feeding three JSON index stores that are read as well as written. Replacing chrono therefore has to parse an existing on-disk corpus, not merely emit a new format. Two facts make the work more tractable than it looks. The repository already owns two chrono-free RFC 3339 formatters, one at second precision and one at nanosecond precision with correct pre-epoch handling, which are duplicated logic and the natural seed for the owned type. And the owned type is genuinely new rather than a rename: the existing Time newtype is nanoseconds but process-epoch relative in its wall-clock fallback, so it is not interchangeable with a UNIX-epoch instant.

alternatives_considered.option: Remove the time crate now, since it has one call site.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Permitted in principle and the plan is right about the scope, but the registry binds time, chrono and std::time to a single capability whose no-claim boundary says a nanoseconds-to-RFC3339 helper is only a foundation and cannot justify removing chrono or time before full public and persisted parity. Removing one while the other remains would also leave two RFC 3339 implementations plus the two already-owned ones, which is more duplication rather than less.

alternatives_considered.option: Replace chrono in place by swapping the field types.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Those ten fields are public and serde-derived, so the swap is a semver-breaking public API change whenever the cli or benchmark-adapters feature is enabled, and it changes the on-disk representation of three JSON index stores that are read back. Nothing currently tests that round-trip in either direction.

alternatives_considered.option: Treat the existing owned RFC 3339 formatters as the replacement.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: They are emit-only. Neither parses, neither does calendar arithmetic, and neither is a serde-stable type. They cover formatting, which is the easy third of the capability, and they are also duplicated between two modules, which is itself worth fixing.

alternatives_considered.option: Reuse the existing Time newtype as the owned UTC instant.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It is nanoseconds, but its wall-clock accessor is process-epoch relative rather than UNIX-epoch, and it deliberately carries no calendar semantics because it exists for scheduling and virtual time. Conflating the two would either corrupt scheduling semantics or produce wrong timestamps.

alternatives_considered.option: Drop the chrono dev-dependency along with the production one.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It is used as an independent differential oracle for PostgreSQL binary temporal decoding. Removing it would remove the reference implementation that proves that decoding correct, which is the opposite of what a replacement campaign needs.

known_gaps.summary: The capability registry names src/time/mod.rs and src/bin/asupersync.rs as source owners. Every file under src/time/ contains zero chrono and zero time-crate references; it is asupersync's own async timer module and appears to have been matched on the word time. The binary is a correct owner for the time crate only. The row names none of the four files that actually own chrono.
known_gaps.consequence: The row's own exposure classification cites public API and persisted format, yet the entire justification for both lives in files it does not list. A baseline built from it would inventory the timer wheel and miss ten public fields and three persisted stores.

known_gaps.summary: There is no round-trip test for any chrono field, and no test at all for the three persisted JSON index stores.
known_gaps.consequence: The registry promises round-trip compatible public and persisted values, and nothing measures it. This is the single largest evidence gap for the capability and the precondition for any type swap.

known_gaps.summary: There are no byte-level goldens for any chrono-serde persisted document. The one frozen golden containing literal RFC 3339 values covers an observability diagnostics schema at second precision, and the CLI output golden scrubs timestamps entirely, so it is format-blind.
known_gaps.consequence: A precision or suffix change in the public serde representation would pass the CLI goldens unnoticed.

known_gaps.summary: The single time-crate call site is covered by exactly one test vector, at a whole-second boundary. There is no leap-year, fractional-second, negative-epoch or range-limit case.
known_gaps.consequence: Even the smallest and best-understood part of the capability lacks the calendar vectors the bead requires.

known_gaps.summary: Nothing owned parses RFC 3339. The two existing owned formatters emit only, and they are duplicated logic across the ATP logging module and the JetStream module at different precisions.
known_gaps.consequence: Reading the existing persisted corpus is unachievable with the current owned code, and consolidating the two formatters is prerequisite work rather than cleanup.

known_gaps.summary: The existing Time newtype is nanoseconds but process-epoch relative in its wall-clock fallback, and deliberately carries no calendar semantics.
known_gaps.consequence: An owned UTC instant is genuinely new work, not a rename or an extension of the existing type. Any plan that assumes otherwise will either corrupt scheduling semantics or produce wrong timestamps.

known_gaps.summary: chrono is used in tests as an independent differential oracle for PostgreSQL binary date, timestamp and interval decoding.
known_gaps.consequence: Removing the dev-dependency would remove the reference implementation that proves that decoding correct. The dev-dependency must outlive the production one.

known_gaps.summary: The plan classifies the time crate as a Phase-2 removal and chrono as Phase-5 owned work, while an earlier audit line proposes consolidating both in Phase 2. The registry binds both plus the standard library clock to one capability with a single disposition, and its no-claim boundary states that a nanoseconds-to-RFC3339 helper cannot justify removing either before full public and persisted parity.
known_gaps.consequence: Three documents disagree about phase and scope. Acting on the Phase-2 framing would remove one crate while leaving the harder half untouched and would add a third RFC 3339 implementation to the two already present.

known_gaps.summary: Neither the registry's baseline command nor any of its three scenario identifiers appears anywhere in the repository.
known_gaps.consequence: The named baseline command exercises nothing for this capability today.

adrs.title: Preserve full user-supplied regex semantics and privacy guarantees; fixed scanners are only a fast path
adrs.decision_summary: The regex crate stays. The source read produced one clarification and one genuine defect. The clarification is that the real regex surface is a single file, the OTLP privacy configuration, where downstream code supplies its own patterns through a public string vector and a public constructor that returns the regex crate's own error type. That error type is a semver-visible leak under the metrics feature. The defect is that the plan's framing of fixed PII scanners as a replacement for the engine does not describe the code: all four built-in detectors are themselves regex-backed today, so there is no non-regex fast path to promote, and the only hand-rolled matching in the privacy path is a Luhn check and a glob matcher. Separately, a module named regex in the ATP chunk artifact is a mock that accepts any pattern and ignores it, compiled unconditionally on non-wasm targets, with a real-looking pattern literal at its call site that has never matched anything. It is not a regex-crate consumer and must not be counted as one; it is a live no-mock-policy violation that the plan already flags for deletion.

alternatives_considered.option: Replace the engine with fixed PII scanners plus a subset matcher that fails closed on unsupported syntax, per the plan.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The registry's no-claim boundary is explicit that fixed scanners are not a general regex engine and may never justify dropping custom user patterns. Downstream code can supply arbitrary patterns today, and a fail-closed subset matcher would reject patterns that currently work. Fail-closed is the right posture for a redaction engine, but rejecting a previously accepted pattern is capability loss rather than safety.

alternatives_considered.option: Promote the four built-in detectors as the non-regex fast path.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: They are not non-regex. Email, SSN and phone are regex literals, and the card detector is a regex candidate scan followed by a hand-rolled Luhn check. Promoting them would mean writing them from scratch, not extracting existing code, and the ordering and exact redaction tokens are pinned by tests.

alternatives_considered.option: Keep the engine but remove the public constructor that leaks the regex error type.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Worth doing eventually, but the leak is how a caller learns that a pattern failed to compile. Removing it without an owned error type would either hide compile failures or force a panic, and the panicking wrapper already exists as the alternative. It belongs with the replacement.

alternatives_considered.option: Treat the ATP chunk artifact module as a second regex consumer and include it in the replacement scope.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It uses no regex crate code at all. Its find implementation ignores the pattern entirely, splitting on whitespace and returning the first token whose dot-separated parts start with a digit. Counting it would inflate the scope and, worse, imply the mock is acceptable.

alternatives_considered.option: Defer the mock deletion until the engine decision is settled.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: They are independent. The mock is a production stub that silently ignores a pattern; deleting it and replacing it with an honest bounded version scanner needs no engine decision and is already a separate tracked item.

preserved_public_symbols.note: The entire real regex surface. try_with_pii_pattern returns the regex crate's own error type, which is the semver-visible leak. pii_patterns is a public vector that downstream may mutate directly, and the matcher detects a stale compiled cache and recompiles, so direct mutation is a supported path pinned by a dedicated test.
Frozen only so the mock's removal is a visible, reviewed change rather than silent drift. This file contains no regex crate code; the local module of the same name shadows the crate at the call site.

preserved_feature_flags.name: regex
preserved_feature_flags.effect: The pattern engine behind the OTLP privacy configuration. Optional, and enabled only through the metrics feature.
preserved_feature_flags.no_tokio_guarantee: The regex crate introduces no tokio edge.

preserved_feature_flags.name: metrics
preserved_feature_flags.effect: The only feature that enables the regex crate directly. It therefore also gates the entire privacy redaction surface, which means a build without metrics has no PII redaction engine at all.
preserved_feature_flags.no_tokio_guarantee: The metrics production graph must have no normal-edge dependency on tokio, per the proof lane frozen by DEP-ADR-003.

preserved_surfaces.note: The capability this ADR exists to protect. Downstream supplies arbitrary patterns either through the fallible constructor or by mutating the public vector directly; both paths compile through the full engine. A downstream consumer fixture exercises the constructor with its own pattern.

Email, SSN, card and phone, applied in that order with distinct redaction tokens. All four are regex-backed, so the bead's fixed-scanner fast path does not exist as non-regex code today. Only the Luhn validity check is hand-rolled.

Owned and regex-free: a wildcard glob matcher, not a pattern engine. An adjacent audit asserts the attribute denylist stays exact-match rather than becoming fuzzy, so this surface must not drift toward regex.

A local module named regex that shadows the crate at its call site. Its constructor accepts any pattern and stores it as dead code, and its find ignores the pattern entirely. Compiled unconditionally on non-wasm targets. Recorded as a defect to be replaced with an honest bounded version scanner, not as a regex consumer.

The bead and the plan both speak of fixed scanners as a fast path in front of the engine. No such non-regex path exists; the detectors are regex literals. Recorded so the plan's phrasing is not mistaken for existing work.
No regex or privacy fuzz target exists, although the fuzz build links the engine and the capability declares an adversarial-limits scenario and a catastrophic-backtracking security invariant.

preserved_wire_contract.protocol: in-process pattern matching and telemetry redaction; not a wire protocol
preserved_wire_contract.encoding: regex crate 1.12 syntax as accepted today
preserved_wire_contract.signal_paths_note: Redaction applies uniformly across metrics, traces and logs through the shared privacy configuration.
preserved_wire_contract.accepted_language: The accepted pattern language is whatever the incumbent engine accepts: full Unicode and byte syntax, flags, classes, captures, boundaries, case folding and leftmost-first semantics. Narrowing it is capability loss even if the narrower engine is safer.
preserved_wire_contract.redaction_tokens: Custom pattern matches yield a generic redaction token; the four built-in detectors yield distinct per-class tokens. Both the tokens and the detector ordering are observable and pinned by tests.

preserved_config_semantics.name: custom_pattern_precedence
preserved_config_semantics.contract: Custom user patterns are evaluated before the built-in detectors, and a custom match yields the generic redaction token rather than a class-specific one.

preserved_config_semantics.name: direct_mutation_support
preserved_config_semantics.contract: Mutating the public vector directly, without going through a constructor, still takes effect: the matcher detects a stale compiled cache and recompiles. This is a supported path with its own test and may not regress into silent no-op behavior.

preserved_config_semantics.name: compile_error_visibility
preserved_config_semantics.contract: An invalid pattern is reported rather than silently dropped. Both a fallible and a panicking constructor exist and both must remain, because silently ignoring a user's privacy pattern is the worst possible failure for this capability.

preserved_config_semantics.name: detector_ordering_and_tokens
preserved_config_semantics.contract: Email, then SSN, then card, then phone, each with its own redaction token. A card candidate that fails the Luhn check is left unredacted, which is pinned by a test.

preserved_config_semantics.surface: field dropping and the allowed-field list
preserved_config_semantics.contract: Field matching is wildcard globbing, not regex, and the attribute denylist is exact-match. Neither may drift toward fuzzy matching.

preserved_config_semantics.name: fail_closed_redaction
preserved_config_semantics.contract: Redaction fails closed: when in doubt, redact. A pattern that cannot be evaluated must not result in unredacted output.

preserved_config_semantics.name: feature_coupling
preserved_config_semantics.contract: The redaction engine is available only with metrics enabled. Any change to that coupling changes whether a build has PII redaction at all and is a security-relevant decision.

The call site passes a real-looking version pattern that has never been used.
